data.title: Understanding Memory Management, Part 5: Fighting with Rust
data.author: Curiositry
data.article_summary: 这篇文章是关于Rust内存管理的系列文章的第五部分，重点讨论了在Rust中进行复杂操作时需要注意的所有权和借用问题。文章通过一个简单的代码示例展示了在使用`for`循环遍历向量时出现的所有权转移错误。具体来说，Rust在调用`into_iter()`时会获取向量`x`的所有权，导致后续无法再次使用`x`。为了避免这个问题，可以使用对向量`x`的引用，即`&x`。文章还解释了Rust中的语法糖以及不同类型的方法调用（如引用、可变引用和所有权转移），并通过进一步的代码示例展示了如何正确使用这些特性。总的来说，文章深入探讨了Rust中所有权和借用的实际应用，帮助开发者更好地理解和解决相关问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust语言的内存管理、函数重载、编译器行为以及与其他语言（如Zig、C++、GC语言）的比较。

不同观点：
• **关于函数重载的技术细节**：
   - steveklabnik指出，Rust不支持传统意义上的函数重载，而是通过trait的不同实现来达到类似效果。这避免了潜在的编译器错误，因为可以明确选择正确的实现。
   - 他还提到，虽然这可能导致编译器报错，但通过手动选择可以避免问题，且这不算作破坏性变更。

• **Rust内存管理的优劣**：
   - teleforce认为，21世纪的编程语言应具备完美的垃圾回收（GC）机制，而不是像Rust那样手动管理内存。他用汽车行业的自动变速箱类比，说明自动化管理应是趋势。
   - Animats则解释了Rust内存管理的核心原则，包括单一所有权和借用检查器的作用，认为理解这些原则后，Rust的设计是合理的。
   - rollcat对比了Zig和Rust的内存管理策略，认为Zig的策略对开发者更友好，但Rust更严格，虽然常常“大喊”（编译错误），但往往是有道理的。

• **Rust编译器和语言复杂性的争议**：
   - diath抱怨即使是简单的"for x in y"循环，Rust也需要复杂的处理，认为这是Rust ergonomics差的表现。
   - cornholio认为Rust将复杂的内存管理强加给程序员，带来的收益（如性能提升）对于非系统编程来说不值得。
   - Surac虽然觉得Rust有些概念过于冗长，但总体上理解了Rust的优点，并计划从Rust中借鉴一些想法用于C/C++开发。
   - gitroom也有类似感受，怀念C的简单，但坚持使用Rust以减少bug。

• **其他技术细节和个人观点**：
   - bsaul指出了一个代码示例中的小错误，关于"`.set_value()`应为`&mut self`而非`&self`"。
   - sidcool简单称赞了文章写得好。
   - dmitrygr则表示不愿意浪费时间在诸如"为什么需要`&x`来修复问题"这样的细节上。

补充讨论：
- Rust的借用检查器和所有权模型是讨论的核心，支持者认为这些特性带来了更高的代码健壮性，反对者则认为这增加了不必要的复杂性。
- 关于Rust与Zig、C++、GC语言的对比也是讨论的一个重点，反映出不同开发者对语言设计和使用体验的不同偏好。
- 总体上，Rust的严格性和编译器“喊叫”是争议的焦点，部分开发者认为这是提高代码质量的必要代价，另一部分则觉得这种复杂性影响了开发体验。

Understanding Memory Management, Part 5: Fighting with Rust
Posted by
ekr
on 20 Apr 2025
This is the fifth post in my planned multipart series on memory
management. You will probably want to go back and read Part
I
, which covers C, parts
II
and
III
, which cover C++, and part
IV
, which introduces Rust memory
management.  In part IV, we got through the basics of Rust memory
management up through smart pointers. In this post I want
to look at some of the gymnastics you need to engage in to do
serious work in Rust.
Unexpected Moves
#
Consider the following simple Rust code:
fn
main
(
)
{
let
x
=
vec!
[
1
,
2
]
;
for
y
in
x
{
println!
(
"{}"
,
y
)
;
}
println!
(
"{}"
,
x
.
len
(
)
)
;
}
This is straightforward: we create a vector containing the values
[1, 2]
, then iterate over it and print each element, and then
finally print out the length of the vector. This is the kind of
code people write every day. Let's see what happens when we compile
it.
Error[E0382]: borrow of moved value: `x`
--> iter_into.rs:7:20
|
2   |     let x = vec![1, 2];
|         - move occurs because `x` has type `Vec
`, which does not implement the `Copy` trait
3   |
4   |     for y in x {
|              - `x` moved due to this implicit call to `.into_iter()`
...
7   |     println!("{}", x.len());
|                    ^ value borrowed here after move
|
note: `into_iter` takes ownership of the receiver `self`, which moves `x`
--> /Users/ekr/.rustup/toolchains/stable-aarch64-apple-darwin/lib/rustlib/src/rust/library/core/src/iter/traits/collect.rs:346:18
|
346 |     fn into_iter(self) -> Self::IntoIter;
|                  ^^^^
help: consider iterating over a slice of the `Vec
`'s content to avoid moving into the `for` loop
|
4   |     for y in &x {
|              +
error: aborting due to 1 previous error
For more information about this error, try `rustc --explain E0382`.
make: *** [iter_into.out] Error 1
No joy! The error message is reasonably helpful, though:
note: `into_iter` takes ownership of the receiver `self`, which moves `x`
At a high level, here is what is happening.
The
for y in x
syntax tells Rust you want an iterator
In order to produce that iterator, Rust calls
x.into_iter()
, defined
by the trait
IntoIterator
which results in an iterator over
i32
.
The iterator
takes ownership
of the input vector
x
.
In the spirit of this series, though, let's dig one level deeper. You can ignore
the rest of this section if you don't really care about Rust details, but this
took me a little while to work out, so it's going up on the Internet.
The
for y in x
expression in Rust is
syntactic
sugar
for creating an iterator. The
x
value must implement the
IntoIterator
trait, which has the method
into_iter()
:
pub
trait
IntoIterator
{
type
Item
;
type
IntoIter
:
Iterator
<
Item
=
Self
::
Item
>
;
// Required method
fn
into_iter
(
self
)
->
Self
::
IntoIter
;
}
.into_iter()
returns an
Iterator
object which exposes a
.next()
method that returns the next value
in the iterator. You can loop over the iterator by calling
.next()
until it returns
None
(see
here
for some background on union types in Rust). For reference, here's what
the Rust reference says is the equivalent code to
for ...
:
{
let
result
=
match
IntoIterator
::
into_iter
(
iter_expr
)
{
mut
iter
=>
'label
:
loop
{
let
mut
next
;
match
Iterator
::
next
(
&
mut
iter
)
{
Option
::
Some
(
val
)
=>
next
=
val
,
Option
::
None
=>
break
,
}
;
let
PATTERN
=
next
;
let
(
)
=
{
/* loop body */
}
;
}
,
}
;
result
}
As the code above says, Rust implicitly calls
IntoIterator::into_iter(x)
,
which is to say it calls the
.into_iter()
method call for
x
(in this
case of type
Vec<i32>
, i.e.,
x.into_iter()
). The
IntoIterator::into_iter()
syntax is
needed in case
x
implements more than one trait that has an
into_iter()
method because we need to tell the Rust compiler which method to choose
(see below).
This syntactic sugar is all internal compiler magic, but from here on in the rest is normal
(though a bit arcane) Rust.
Function Overloads
#
So why does this result in a move and why does replacing
x
with
&x
fix it?
If you've done any Rust programming, you know that you can call a method that
takes any kind of
self
parameter (i.e., a moved object, a reference, or a mutable
reference) as
self.foo
and Rust will automatically produce the right kind of parameter
assuming your object is compatible in terms of mutability.
For instance:
Code
#
struct
X
{
}
impl
X
{
fn
ref_method
(
&
self
)
{
println!
(
"ref"
)
;
}
fn
mut_ref_method
(
&
mut
self
)
{
println!
(
"mut_ref"
)
;
}
fn
move_method
(
self
)
{
println!
(
"move"
)
;
}
}
fn
main
(
)
{
let
mut
x
=
X
{
}
;
let
mut
y
=
X
{
}
;
let
yref
=
&
mut
y
;
x
.
ref_method
(
)
;
x
.
mut_ref_method
(
)
;
x
.
move_method
(
)
;
// x.move_method();     Does not compile
yref
.
ref_method
(
)
;
yref
.
mut_ref_method
(
)
;
// yref.move_method();  Does not compile
(
&
y
)
.
ref_method
(
)
;
(
&
mut
y
)
.
mut_ref_method
(
)
;
}
Output
#
ref
mut_ref
move

data.title: Cuttlefish 'talk' with their arms, study reveals
data.author: geox
data.article_summary: 科学家发现乌贼通过独特的腕部动作进行交流，这些被称为“腕波信号”的动作包括“向上”、“侧面”、“翻滚”和“皇冠”四种姿态，每种姿态涉及不同的腕部位置和波动模式，常伴有体色变化。研究显示，这些信号可以通过视觉和水中振动被感知，形成多感官交流系统。乌贼对正放的视频信号反应更强烈，且能区分原始信号和被扰乱的信号。该发现揭示了乌贼复杂的交流方式，可能涉及侧线和平衡囊等感知水运动的器官，为进一步理解海洋无脊椎动物的交流提供了新视角。

43904478.article_content:
ig. 1. Four distinct arm wave signs observed in adult Sepia officinalis (A–D) and juvenile Sepia bandensis (E–H):
“Up” sign (A, E): The most frequently displayed gesture, characterized by upward extension of the first arm pair and outward extension of the fourth pair, while the second and third arm pairs are twisted at the midsection.
“Side” sign (B, F): All arms are rolled to one side of the body, creating a lateral display.
“Roll” sign (C, G): All arms are tucked and rolled beneath the head, altering its shape to highlight the eyes.
“Crown” sign (D, H): Features a rapid “spitting” motion, with arms arranged in a crown-like formation.
Scientists have discovered that cuttlefish use distinct arm movements to communicate with each other, adding another dimension to these already remarkable marine creatures.
Researchers from the École Normale Supérieure in Paris and the Italian Institute of Technology have identified specific arm gestures they’ve named “arm wave signs” that appear to serve as a communication system between cuttlefish. The study, published this month in bioRxiv, reveals that these underwater signals can be perceived both visually and through water vibrations – essentially creating a multi-sensory conversation.
According to the researchers, this newly discovered behavior involves distinct arm movements that follow specific patterns in two cuttlefish species. These arm wave signs involve deliberate, expressive arm undulations that can last several seconds and be combined in various sequences.
The research team, led by Sophie Cohen-Bodénès and Peter Neri, documented these movements over months of observation. They identified four distinct gestures they named “up,” “side,” “roll,” and “crown” signs. Each movement involves different arm positions and undulating motions, often combined with color changes on the cuttlefish’s skin.
What makes this discovery particularly intriguing is that the cuttlefish responded differently to these signals depending on their orientation. When shown videos of other cuttlefish performing these arm waves, the animals were significantly more likely to “wave back” when the video was displayed right-side up versus upside-down – similar to how humans perceive faces and other socially relevant displays.
But perhaps most surprisingly, the researchers found evidence that these arm motions might be perceived not just visually but also through vibrations in the water. Using specially designed playback experiments, they recorded the mechanical waves produced by these arm movements and played them back to test subjects.
The researchers found that these signals work through multiple sensory channels. By using specialized playback experiments, they demonstrated that cuttlefish can perceive these communications both visually and through water movement detection.
The cuttlefish were more responsive to the original recordings compared to versions that were played backward or scrambled – suggesting they could detect meaningful information in these water movements.
This dual-channel communication system might utilize the cuttlefish’s lateral line and statocysts, sensory organs that detect water movement and low-frequency vibrations. These findings suggest an intriguing parallel between cephalopod communication and the audiovisual communication seen in vertebrates – despite evolving independently.
The team points to fascinating evolutionary parallels, suggesting that just as cephalopods independently evolved camera-like eyes similar to vertebrates, their sensory systems for detecting water movement may have evolved to serve communication functions similar to vertebrate hearing.
The exact meaning behind these arm signs remains unclear. The researchers observed them in various contexts – during mating, hunting, defensive situations, and sometimes spontaneously. This suggests the signs might serve multiple purposes depending on the situation.
The discovery opens new avenues for understanding communication in marine invertebrates and adds to our appreciation of cephalopod intelligence. These surprisingly sophisticated “conversations” taking place beneath the waves highlight how much we still have to learn about communication in the animal kingdom.
Looking ahead, the research team hopes to explore how this discovery might provide insights into communication between vastly different animal species, potentially opening new pathways for understanding how diverse creatures interact with their environment.

• [go_elmo] 认为跨物种的交流问题普遍存在，科学证实了植物、真菌、哺乳动物甚至乌贼之间都有复杂的交流方式，人类并不是独一无二的。
• [97-109-107] 提到Peter Watts的小说《盲视》中，外星生物"Scramblers"表现出高度智能和复杂行为但没有意识，这可能与乌贼的交流方式有相似之处。
• [nfgrep] 提到《The Mountain in The Sea》一书，暗示乌贼的交流复杂性正逐渐被科学证实，类似于小说情节。
• [A_D_E_P_T] 认为不应食用乌贼和大型章鱼，因为它们高度智能且具有游戏性，显示出对动物保护的关注。
• [damnitbuilds] 以讽刺的口吻质疑通过手指敲击桌子是否也算作交流，可能是在质疑对乌贼交流方式的解读。

补充讨论：
• [NonHyloMorph] 以幽默方式提到乌贼与"意大利人"共享某些特征，暗指乌贼交流中的肢体语言特性。
• [asmodeuslucifer] 分享了个人经验，描述了一次在水下与乌贼互动的情景，强调乌贼具有伪装能力。
• [enneff] 也分享了个人潜水经历，提到与乌贼进行长时间的眼神接触，认为乌贼可能具有复杂的认知能力。
• [kozlovsky] 提出乌贼的肢体信号是否构成某种语言的字母表，提出了对乌贼交流系统性的疑问。
• [CoopaTroopa] 以玩笑方式重复了乌贼与意大利人的类比。
• [CommenterPerson] 表示因鱼类、鸟类和哺乳动物的感知能力而转向素食，显示出对动物福利的关注。
• [hartjer] 以幽默方式表达了对讨论内容与预期不符的失望。

争议焦点：
• 乌贼的肢体动作是否构成一种语言，以及如何科学地解读这些动作的含义。
• 对人与动物（特别是乌贼）之间复杂交流的理解与定义存在不同看法。

data.title: Curl: We still have not seen a valid security report done with AI help
data.author: indigodaddy
data.article_summary: Daniel Stenberg, CEO of curl, 表达了对HackerOne平台上大量低质量AI生成的安全报告的不满。他宣布，将要求每个提交报告的人说明是否使用了AI生成报告，并对被认为是AI粗制滥造的报告提交者立即封禁。Stenberg提到，他们尚未看到任何有效的AI辅助安全报告，且这种现象已接近DDoS攻击的程度。他考虑过通过要求提交者支付保证金来提高报告质量，并对AI生成垃圾报告进行过滤。其他用户也提出了类似的担忧和建议，如建立全球黑名单或白名单，以及利用GPT管道处理报告等。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI生成内容对漏洞报告质量和安全研究工作的影响

不同观点：
• **danielvf**：认为当前的LLM（大型语言模型）生成的漏洞报告大多是无效的，且用户会反复使用LLM处理反馈，导致生成更无意义的内容。他质疑人们是否能区分有效信息和垃圾信息，并认为AI工具目前还不能有效用于安全研究。

• **bogwog**：提出恶意使用AI生成大量无效报告可能会成为一种攻击手段，目的是通过DDOS方式掩盖真实漏洞，从而减少被发现的可能性。

• **vessenes**：认为AI正在改变这一领域的经济模式，并提出建立声誉系统以区分高质量报告和垃圾报告。通过给予通过身份验证的用户更多权限，鼓励他们提交有效报告。

• **parliament32**：同意AI生成的报告多为无稽之谈，并指出一些具体例子，如报告中的函数名根本不存在，批评这些报告未经核实。

• **kazinator**：建议对报告者收取可退还的押金，以减少无效报告的数量。如果报告是真实的或诚实错误，押金将退还；如果是无效的，则不退还。

• **rdtsc**：引用报告中的例子，指出报告者在报告中表明自己开放就业，讽刺他们使用AI生成垃圾报告的行为。

• **uludag**：指出LLM在处理代码安全漏洞时，往往会编造不存在的信息，认为这是系统对齐问题，限制了这些工具的有效性。

• **jacksnipe**：批评那些依赖AI工具的人，常常直接引用AI的回复而不加以理解，认为这种行为毫无帮助。

• **meindnoch**：提出简单解决方案，要求报告者在提交安全报告前支付小额押金，如果报告被认为是AI生成的垃圾，则押金归审查者所有。

• **ianbutler**：提出反例，指出其团队使用AI工具成功发现有效漏洞，并认为问题在于使用者背景和工具调校，而非工具本身。

• **prettyblocks**：质疑如果有人使用AI发现了有效安全问题并成功报告，如何判断AI是否参与其中，认为不应简单否定AI的潜力。

补充讨论：
• 对LinkedIn访问的讨论（molticrystal）：提到对替代界面的需求，以避免登录访问LinkedIn内容，并分享了相关帖子内容。

争议焦点：
• AI生成内容对安全研究的影响：一方面认为AI生成大量无效报告，严重干扰正常工作；另一方面认为AI工具若正确使用，可以发现有效漏洞。
• 如何有效筛选和激励高质量报告：提出押金制度、声誉系统等不同解决方案，以应对AI生成垃圾报告的问题。

总结：评论主要围绕AI生成报告的有效性和其对安全研究工作的影响展开讨论，争议点在于如何平衡AI工具的潜力和其带来的问题。

data.title: Is Planet Nine Alone in the Outer System?
data.author: JPLeRouzic
data.article_summary:
文章探讨了假设存在的第九行星及其在太阳系外围的探索潜力。作者引用Robert Browning的名言，引出人类探索太空边界的渴望，并提到目前对太阳引力透镜距离（约550 AU）的探索。尽管这一目标超出当前技术能力，但JPL的团队正在进行相关任务设计。文章指出，寻找如第九行星这样的新目标可能激发更多探索兴趣，尤其是如果它类似于在其他星系中发现的超级地球或迷你海王星。

研究显示，许多恒星系统存在超级地球，这支持了第九行星存在的可能性。其质量预计为地球的10倍以上，半长轴约700 AU。尽管光学调查未能发现，但通过比较IRAS和AKARI卫星23年间的数据，研究团队尝试寻找可能的红外源，以确认第九行星的存在。文章强调，尽管技术挑战大，但发现新行星将极大推动太空探索。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：太阳系外围异常轨道成因的解释及假设行星的存在

不同观点：
• adrian_b认为，许多跨海王星天体的奇异轨道并不能直接证明目前在海王星之外存在一个巨大的行星。他认为，这仅表明过去曾有一个大质量天体（可能是一颗经过的恒星）扰动了这些轨道，并引用了2024年发表的相关论文支持其观点。
• Qem提到了Brown的观点，即现有观测到的某些天体不太可能是假定的第九行星，因为其轨道倾斜度与预测不符。同时，Qem还提到了Lykawka和Mukai提出的独立假设，认为可能存在另一个未被发现的大质量天体，与Batygin和Brown提出的第九行星假设不同。
• yellowapple的观点更多是对冥王星降级的情感反应，并幽默地表达了对不能将假定的跨冥王星天体称为"X行星"的失望。

补充讨论：
• rdtsc提供了之前讨论的链接和一个相关论文的链接，但未提出新的论点。
• p0w3n3d和WalterBright以幽默方式回应，没有提出实质性观点。
• glimshe抱怨网站劫持滚动条，属于技术问题，与讨论主题无关。
• codethief指出了原文中未标明来源的问题，并提供了Mike Brown相关帖子的链接。
• xhrpost进行了技术性讨论，计算了使用Dark Energy Camera进行后续观测的可能分辨率。
• ArthurStacks认为这个话题已经讨论了几十年，但没有提出新的论据。
• soufron询问了关于过去某恒星经过的 proposed timeline。
• RajT88和eth0up以幽默方式表达了对假定行星形状和大小的猜测。
• cratermoon重申了冥王星是最大的跨海王星天体之一的观点。
• Hobadee以幽默方式坚持认为第九行星就是冥王星。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于太阳系外围异常轨道的成因：是一颗过去经过的恒星（adrian_b的观点）还是一个未被发现的大质量天体（Qem引用的Lykawka和Mukai的观点），亦或是广泛讨论的第九行星假设（Brown等人的观点）。
• 冥王星的地位问题再次被幽默地提及（Hobadee的观点），但并非严肃的科学讨论。

43907586.article_content:
Is Planet Nine Alone in the Outer System?
by
Paul Gilster
|
May 6, 2025
|
Outer Solar System
|
2 comments
It was Robert Browning who said “Ah, but a man’s reach should exceed his grasp, or what’s a heaven for?” A rousing thought, but we don’t always know where we should reach. In terms of space exploration, a distant but feasible target is the solar gravitational lens distance beginning around 550 AU. So far the SGL definitely exceeds our grasp, but solid work in mission design by Slava Turyshev and team is ongoing at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory.
Targets need to tantalize, and maybe a target that we hadn’t previously considered is now emerging. Planet Nine, the hypothesized world that may lurk somewhere in our Solar System’s outer reaches, would be such an extraordinary discovery that it would tempt future mission designers in the same way.
This is interesting because right now our deep space targets need to be well defined. I love the idea of
Interstellar Probe
, the craft designed at JHU/APL, but it’s hard to excite the public with the idea of looking back at the heliosphere from the outside (although the science return would be fabulous). Pluto was hard enough to sell to the powers that be, but Allen Stern and team got the job done because they had a whole world that had never been seen up close. Will Planet Nine, if found, turn out to be the destination that some budget-strapped team finds a way to explore?
We have a lot to learn about planetary demographics given that our planet-finding technologies work best for larger worlds closer in to their stars. But a recent microlensing study suggests that as many as one out of every three stars in our galaxy should host a super-Earth in a Jupiter-like orbit (citation below). Microlensing is helpful because it can reveal planets at large distances from their parent stars. Super-Earths appear to be abundant. If it exists, Planet Nine isn’t in a Jovian orbit, but it’s probably smaller than Neptune.
In so many ways this planet makes sense. We’ve found planets like it in innumerable stellar systems. We also know that mechanisms of gravitational slingshotting can push a planet either out of its system entirely or into an entirely new orbit, explaining our prior lack of detection. We’re talking about a planet on the order of a super-Earth or a mini-Neptune, the former larger than our planet but still rocky, the latter smaller than Neptune but gaseous.
Image:
An illustration shows what Planet Nine might look like orbiting far from our Sun. We have found many such worlds around other stars, but finding one in our own backyard is taking time because of its distance and an orbit that is probably well off the ecliptic. Assuming a planet is there at all. Image credit: NASA/Caltech.
The evidence in the orbits of a number of outer system objects points to something perturbing their paths, and seems to implicate something big. Now we have, after years of evidence gathering and debate, at least a possible candidate for this world. In process at
Publications of the Astronomical Society of Australia (PASA)
, although not yet published, the paper digs deep into data from the Infrared Astronomical Satellite as well as AKARI, a Japanese satellite somewhat more sensitive than IRAS and launched in 2006.
The distant Sedna and other similar bodies with unusual orbital characteristics tell us that something has to account for their high eccentricity and inclination, while a number of Kuiper Belt objects seem to be similarly affected, as shown in the orientation of their orbits (described through what is known as the
argument of perihelion
). Computations thus far indicate mass on the order of something equal to or greater than 10 Earth masses, with a semi-major axis of about 700 AU.
Image:
The six most distant known objects in the solar system with orbits exclusively beyond Neptune (magenta) all mysteriously line up in a single direction. Moreover, when viewed in 3-D, the orbits of all these icy little objects are tilted in the same direction, away from the plane of the solar system. PL-Caltech/R. Hurt.
A huge amount of work has gone into this analysis, all ably summarized in the paper, which comes from Terry Long Phan (National Tsing Hua University, Taiwan) and colleagues. Optical surveys have heretofore failed to find this object, but 700 AU is fully 23 times the distance of Neptune from the Sun, far enough out that visible wavelengths need to give way to infrared to find it.
Phan’s team looked for candidate objects in the range of 500 to 700 AU using the two far-infrared surveys mentioned above, which are both all-sky in range but separated by 23 years, making for useful comparisons. The idea was to find an object that moved from an IRAS position to an AKARI position after those 23 years. 文章探讨了假设存在的第九行星及其在太阳系外围的探索潜力。作者引用Robert Browning的名言，引出人类探索太空边界的渴望，并提到目前对太阳引力透镜距离（约550 AU）的探索。尽管这一目标超出当前技术能力，但JPL的团队正在进行相关任务设计。文章指出，寻找如第九行星这样的新目标可能激发更多探索兴趣，尤其是如果它类似于在其他星系中发现的超级地球或迷你海王星。

研究显示，许多恒星系统存在超级地球，这支持了第九行星存在的可能性。其质量预计为地球的10倍以上，半长轴约700 AU。尽管光学调查未能发现，但通过比较IRAS和AKARI卫星23年间的数据，研究团队尝试寻找可能的红外源，以确认第九行星的存在。文章强调，尽管技术挑战大，但发现新行星将极大推动太空探索。

不同观点：
• adrian_b认为，许多跨海王星天体的奇异轨道并不能直接证明目前在海王星之外存在一个巨大的行星。他认为，这仅表明过去曾有一个大质量天体（可能是一颗经过的恒星）扰动了这些轨道，并引用了2024年发表的相关论文支持其观点。
• Qem提到了Brown的观点，即现有观测到的某些天体不太可能是假定的第九行星，因为其轨道倾斜度与预测不符。同时，Qem还提到了Lykawka和Mukai提出的独立假设，认为可能存在另一个未被发现的大质量天体，与Batygin和Brown提出的第九行星假设不同。
• yellowapple的观点更多是对冥王星降级的情感反应，并幽默地表达了对不能将假定的跨冥王星天体称为"X行星"的失望。

data.author: dsevil
data.article_summary: "Old Timey Mono" 是一种基于1906年 Reproducing Typewriter 字体设计的等宽字体，专为提升可读性和避免复制失真设计，适合编码和剧本写作。它包括常规版和代码专用版，后者具有更易辨识的字符设计。该字体支持广泛的语言和字符集，包括拉丁字母、西里尔字母和希腊字母，并涵盖多种 Unicode 区块。字体适用于多种操作系统，并为不同环境提供了字体平滑建议。该项目文件包含源代码、二进制文件和相关资源，用户可以从发布页面下载。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一款名为 Old Timey Mono 的字体的特点、使用场景及改进建议

不同观点：
• **[dsevil]** 介绍 Old Timey Mono 及其变体 Old Timey Code，指出该字体源自1906年的字体 Reproducing Typewriter，并经过改进以提高小字号下的可读性，特别适用于编码场景。该用户提供了字体的下载链接，并邀请其他人提出意见。

• **[Telemakhos]** 对字体支持的多语言特性（如希腊语和拉丁语扩展）表示赞赏，但提出了一些技术性建议：包括组合变音符号的支持（如在拉丁 y 上加 breve）、调整重叠变音符号的高度，以及改进某些希腊字母（如 η 和 ζ）上的重音符号位置。此外，还建议考虑添加 Porsonic 或单曲线型的 circumflex 变体。

• **[JohnDeHope]** 对字体的现代适用性提出疑问，尤其是对于编码场景。建议将乘法符号 * 与其它数学运算符（如 +、-、~）对齐，并建议调整 # 符号的设计以更好地融入其他标点符号。

• **[kleiba]** 指出该字体未包含德语的 ß 字母，导致不支持德语，质疑为何德语未被支持，而卢森堡语却得到了支持。

• **[psunavy03]** 试用了编码版本后，建议增加点状零的选项，认为这样能提高可读性。

• **[plumbees]** 报告了在 Windows 系统上字体文件无法正常使用的问题，期待下一版本的改进。

• **[mhd]** 提到自己喜欢类似风格的 Letter Gothic 12 Pitch 字体，表示会尝试 Old Timey Mono。

• **[evan_piermont]** 询问是否有简单的方法将该字体集成到 LaTeX 中作为数学字体使用。

• **[kaitocross]** 同样对卢森堡语支持而德语不支持表示困惑。

• **[olelele]** 简单表达了对字体的喜爱，并表示会使用该字体。

补充讨论：
- 字体的多语言支持（特别是德语和希腊语）是讨论的一个焦点，用户对变音符号和特定字符的显示效果提出了具体建议。
- 针对编码场景的优化也是讨论的重点，包括符号对齐和特定字符设计上的改进。
- 有用户报告了字体在 Windows 系统上的兼容性问题，表明可能存在技术上的改进空间。
- 最后，有用户询问该字体在 LaTeX 中的使用方法，显示出对该字体在学术和技术文档中应用的兴趣。

SPECIMEN
https://webonastick.com/fonts/old-timey-mono/
About
A clean monospace typeface based on Reproducing Typewriter which was
available as early as 1906.  Reproducing Typewriter was designed for
simulating typewritten letters in smaller point sizes for
advertisements, catalogs, etc., where readability and/or distortion
resulting from duplication were issues with faces based on actual
typewriters at the time.
"Sight Saver" typewriter faces designed for readability were also
available, though they were at larger sizes than ordinary pica or
elite typefaces.
I developed Old Timey Mono because I thought those characteristics
would make it a good basis for a coding font with an antique
aesthetic.  You may have seen Reproducing Typewriter used in the
Turbo Pascal 3.0
product manual.
At a size of 12pt (6 lines per inch), Old Timey Mono is a pica font,
or 10 characters per inch, like Courier.  It
should
be suitable
for screenplay writing.
Code Variant
Along with Old Timey Mono, there is Old Timey Code.  It has a slashed
zero, disambiguated digit one, selected punctuation marks made larger,
and a few certain small letters modified.
Mintty Users
Text -> Font Smoothing -> Partial.  I wish I didn't have to tell you
to do this.
Character Set Coverage
Extensive coverage of Latin, Cyrillic, and Greek scripts.  Language
support is detailed below.
Includes the following sets of characters in their entirety (excepting
controls):
ASCII
ISO-8859-1
Code Page 437
Code Page 850
Windows Glyph List 4 (WGL4)
Adobe Glyph List for New Fonts (AGLFN)
Windows 1252's additional characters
Mac OS Roman, except for the ff and fi ligatures (which don't belong in monospace fonts)
The following Unicode blocks in their entirety:
U+2500–U+257F Box Drawing
U+2580–U+259F Block Elements
U+2800–U+28FF Braille Patterns
U+0100–U+017F Latin Extended-A
And then some.
And a few extras!
Languages Supported
At least according to
https://googlefonts.github.io/shaperglot/
.  As
in, I dragged the font there and copied the list of languages it had
yellow or green indicating full coverage.

data.title: Jury orders NSO to pay $167M for hacking WhatsApp users
data.author: Bender
data.article_summary: WhatsApp has won a major legal victory against Israeli firm NSO Group, receiving $167 million in punitive damages and $444 million in compensatory damages. NSO was found liable for exploiting a WhatsApp vulnerability to install its Pegasus spyware on roughly 1,400 devices, targeting journalists, activists, and government officials. The "clickless" exploit allowed NSO to hack phones via a simple call. Despite NSO's defense that it only sells to governments for law enforcement, the court ruled against the company. This case marks a significant win for privacy advocates and sets a potential legal precedent against spyware companies. NSO's practices were further exposed through the litigation process.
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：NSO Group被判赔偿WhatsApp 1.67亿美元的事件及其相关争议

不同观点：
• IG_Semmelweiss认为，NSO Group被美国政府列入实体清单，已经无法参与美国银行网络，因此WhatsApp的判决对NSO在美国境内的资产没有实际影响。该评论提到了NSO在2017年有约500名员工，并引用了维基百科的资料作为论据。

• jimnotgym指出，出售应用程序漏洞的人应该面临刑事制裁，并质疑为何自己如果做同样的事会入狱，而NSO却没有受到类似惩罚。

• OsrsNeedsf2P对NSO Group向不良客户出售漏洞表示不满，但同时也认为应用程序的安全不应依赖法律强制执行，提出安全应由技术本身保障。

• walterbell提供了Meta发布的证词副本链接，似乎是在补充说明案件的相关文件和证据。

• autoexec以讽刺的口吻评论该判决，认为这对黑客来说是一个好消息，因为他们可以预见如果被抓住，他们的利润会如何受到影响。

• Glyptodon提出另一个角度，质疑如果应用程序本身存在漏洞，用户是否也会责怪其开发者。

• nashashmi提到以色列国防部批准Pegasus软件的销售和使用，暗示以色列政府的支持可能影响NSO的运营。

• Alex_001认为这是对间谍软件滥用的财务问责，但对赔偿金额是否对NSO有实质影响表示怀疑，因为NSO有财力雄厚的客户支持。

• ebfe1以幽默方式质疑如何能从1.67亿美元中分得一部分，暗示普通用户难以从这样的判决中获益。

• b8指出NSO位于以色列，因此不太可能支付赔偿，并提到Zerodium逐渐停止公开活动，暗示美国政府曾购买其漏洞用于针对高价值目标。

• bn-l评论大公司获得司法正义的现象，并提到陪审团还判给WhatsApp 4.44亿美元的补偿性赔偿。

• jeisc认为间谍软件不应合法出售，提出需要的人应自行开发而不是购买现成产品。

• rpgwaiter好奇1.67亿美元中有多少会分给约1400名已知的受害者。

• TZubiri认为此事件像一个政治炸弹，猜测NSO可能不会支付赔偿，除非以色列政府干预并救助。

• aussieguy1234询问赔偿是归于Meta还是黑客行为的受害者。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点包括NSO是否会真正支付赔偿，美国政府和以色列政府在其中的角色，以及应用程序安全应如何保障。
• 评论中多次提到以色列政府对NSO的支持以及美国政府对相关公司的制裁和利用。
• 另一个值得注意的点是对不同主体应承担的责任和法律制裁的讨论，包括开发者、出售者和使用者。

A jury has awarded WhatsApp $167 million in punitive damages in a case the company brought against Israel-based NSO Group for exploiting a software vulnerability that hijacked the phones of thousands of users.
The verdict, reached Tuesday, comes as a major victory not just for Meta-owned WhatsApp but also for privacy- and security-rights advocates who have long criticized the practices of NSO and other exploit sellers. The jury also awarded WhatsApp $444 million in compensatory damages.
Clickless exploit
WhatsApp sued NSO
in 2019
for an attack that targeted roughly 1,400 mobile phones belonging to attorneys, journalists, human-rights activists, political dissidents, diplomats, and senior foreign government officials. NSO, which works on behalf of governments and law enforcement authorities in various countries, exploited a critical WhatsApp vulnerability that allowed it to install NSO’s proprietary spyware
Pegasus
on iOS and Android devices. The clickless exploit worked by placing a call to a target's app. A target did not have to answer the call to be infected.
“Today’s verdict in WhatsApp’s case is an important step forward for privacy and security as the first victory against the development and use of illegal spyware that threatens the safety and privacy of everyone,” WhatsApp said in a
statement
. “Today, the jury’s decision to force NSO, a notorious foreign spyware merchant, to pay damages is a critical deterrent to this malicious industry against their illegal acts aimed at American companies and the privacy and security of the people we serve.”
NSO created WhatsApp accounts in 2018 and used them a year later to initiate calls that exploited the critical vulnerability on phones, which, among others, included 100 members of "civil society" from 20 countries, according to an investigation research group Citizen Lab performed on behalf of WhatsApp. The calls passed through WhatsApp servers and injected malicious code into the memory of targeted devices. The targeted phones would then use WhatsApp servers to connect to malicious servers maintained by NSO.
After discovering the attack, WhatsApp shut them down with a software update that patched the critical vulnerability and notified target users that their devices had been hacked. In the weeks following, Facebook and WhatsApp also kicked NSO employees off their platforms.
WhatsApp’s lawsuit was unprecedented at the time because it was among the first to take aim at the unregulated industry selling sophisticated malware services to governments around the world. NSO argued that it should be immune from such legal actions because it sold tools solely to licensed government intelligence and law-enforcement agencies for use in fighting terrorism, child sex abuse, and other serious crimes. The company said it barred customers from using the tools against human-rights activists, journalists, and dissidents. NSO also said it acted as a check against strongly encrypted platforms that could be used as a haven for criminals.
Tuesday’s verdict—from a jury empaneled by the US District Court for the Northern District of California—is a sharp rebuke of NSO’s defense.
“Turns out regular people don't like companies that help dictators hack dissidents,” John Scott-Railton, a senior researcher at Citizen Lab,
wrote
on Bluesky. “NSO had all the fancy legal arguments. And all the PR spin. But when their conduct got laid bare... the jury sent a massive Monsanto-style punitive damages signal. Other spyware companies: you may be next.”
Besides setting a possible precedent for hacking victims and their technology providers, WhatsApp’s suit exposed NSO practices the company had long tried to keep secret. Last year, the judge hearing the case
ordered
NSO to reveal some of the source code that makes its products work. The litigation also exposed who some of NSO’s customers were and the location of many of the targeted WhatsApp users.
NSO Group didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.

43911167.article_summary: WhatsApp has won a major legal victory against Israeli firm NSO Group, receiving $167 million in punitive damages and $444 million in compensatory damages. NSO was found liable for exploiting a WhatsApp vulnerability to install its Pegasus spyware on roughly 1,400 devices, targeting journalists, activists, and government officials. The "clickless" exploit allowed NSO to hack phones via a simple call. Despite NSO's defense that it only sells to governments for law enforcement, the court ruled against the company. This case marks a significant win for privacy advocates and sets a potential legal precedent against spyware companies. NSO's practices were further exposed through the litigation process.

data.author: celltalk
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：语言学习工具的优化与改进

不同观点：
• [kriro] 建议增加一个无需注册即可生成小故事的体验层，以吸引用户在注册前尝试。
• [jasonpeacock] 提到了类似的工具 Prismatext，它将新语言融入母语书籍中，提供情境学习。
• [DHolzer] 认为应提前告知用户登录要求，并准备好几个演示故事，以节省成本。
• [endofreach] 分享了自己在国外通过购买儿童书籍或双语书籍学习语言的经验。
• [celltalk] 描述了自己和朋友在学习荷兰语时遇到的困难，并介绍了他们开发的 DuoBook 工具，通过 AI 辅助生成双语故事。

补充讨论：
• [999900000999] 认为当前产品只是多个现有技术的组合，建议聚焦于3-4种语言，并增加顾问和基础游戏化/测验功能。
• [hliyan] 提到在自己的母语（僧伽罗语）中发现许多错误，建议增加单词高亮和翻译功能。
• [dustincoates] 建议为希伯来语初学者增加 niqqud（元音符号），并改进语音文本转换（STT）功能。
• [hs586] 分享了自己类似的想法，希望使用已有双语文本的书籍，并提出对句子对齐的要求。
• [dinkblam] 认为故事长度较短，并建议增加逐字翻译或点击单词查看翻译的功能。
• [hejsansvejsan] 报告了一个 bug，瑞典语文本被误读为法语。
• [ErigmolCt] 对 AI 翻译的质量表示担忧，尤其是对于某些语言对。
• [ordzo] 在使用冰岛语时发现语法错误。
• [flipchart] 建议将葡萄牙语分为欧洲和巴西两种版本。
• [outside1234] 提到自己使用 Apple Books 进行类似的语言学习方法。

争议焦点：
- 当前工具的用户体验和功能实现存在争议，包括登录要求、故事长度、翻译准确性等。
- 对 AI 翻译质量的担忧，尤其是在处理小语种和复杂语言对时的表现。
- 用户对产品开发方向的建议不一，有的建议聚焦少数几种语言，有的希望增加更多语言和功能。

data.article_summary: 文章讨论了美国血液制品出口占总商品出口的比例，特别是血浆。文章引用了《经济学人》的数据，指出2024年美国血液制品出口占总商品出口的1.8%，价值370亿美元，成为第九大商品出口项，超过煤炭和黄金。然而，作者对该数据的准确性提出质疑，并通过美国贸易委员会的数据自行计算。根据作者的分析，2023年直接涉及人类血液的产品出口约占总商品出口的0.53%。此外，还有一些类别可能包含血液成分，总计约1.38%。文章强调了数据的复杂性和获取精确信息的困难。

主要讨论点：美国血液出口及其相关数据分析

不同观点：
• blakesterz认为，获取美国贸易委员会网站的数据体验较差，网站速度慢、操作繁琐，且有时会无故无法提供结果，重新提交查询后还会被暂时封锁。
• mehulashah对美国血液出口比例感到惊讶，质疑为何要从美国进口血液而非在本地获取，同时对公共数据的可获取性和详细程度表示赞赏，但质疑Deep Research工具在分析原始数据方面的能力。
• boesboes提到在一些地区献血是非法的，并指出自己献血时需要付出大量时间和精力，而相关机构则通过血液获取高额利润。
• ParacelsusOfEgg澄清了关于美国血液买卖的误解，指出血浆可以出售，但红细胞和血小板不能由献血者出售。
• ilikecakeandpie通过播客介绍了美国血液行业的缺乏监管以及由此带来的公共健康问题，特别是对囚犯的剥削。
• weinzierl认为血液占总出口的0.5%已经很多，并指出2023年美国商品出口占总出口的三分之二。
• declan_roberts担心美国拥有欧洲38%的血液作为贸易谈判筹码，对欧洲不利。
• fmsf对血液关税感到有趣，并期待看到关税对市场的影响，同时宣传了自己的网站。
• thimkerbell批评了论坛链接标题缺乏信息量，呼吁发帖者提高标题质量。
• andai分享了另一个感兴趣的文章链接。
• makmanalp解释了国际贸易编码系统中的分类错误如何导致数据误解，并提供了相关示例和解决方案。
• aezell幽默地表示文章中缺少吸血鬼相关的玩笑。
• ch33zer询问献血是否可能被出售以获取利润，无论是在海外还是其他地方。
• aeternum赞赏文章，并询问是否存在专注于数据分析的文章聚合平台。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于美国血液出口的合理性以及血液买卖的伦理问题。
• 讨论中多次提到数据获取和分析工具的局限性，特别是Deep Research工具在处理原始数据方面的不足。
• 有人对贸易数据分类系统的复杂性和可能的误解进行了详细解释。
• 对血液行业缺乏监管和历史上的公共健康问题也有所关注，特别是通过具体案例和播客进行讨论。

So much blood
So much blood
May 2025
Comments at
lemmy
,
substack
.
In a recent post about
trading stuff for money
, I mentioned:
Europe had a [blood plasma] shortage of around 38%, which it met by importing plasma from paid donors in the United States, where blood products account for 2% of
all
exports by value.
The internet’s reaction was: “TWO PERCENT?” “
TWO PERCENT OF U.S. EXPORTS ARE BLOOD!?
”
Well, I took that 2% number from a 2024
article in the Economist
:
Last year American blood-product exports accounted for 1.8% of the country’s total goods exports, up from just 0.5% a decade ago—and were worth $37bn. That makes blood the country’s ninth-largest goods export, ahead of coal and gold. All told, America now supplies 70% or so of the plasma used to make medicine.
I figured the Economist was trustworthy on matters of economics. But note:
That 1.8% number is for blood
products
, not just blood.
It’s a percentage of
goods
exported, excluding services.
It’s wrong.
The article doesn’t explain how they arrived at 1.8%. And since the Economist speaks in the voice of God (without bylines), I can’t corner and harass the actual journalist. I’d have liked to reverse-engineer their calculations, but this was impossible since the world hasn’t yet caught on that they should always
show lots of digits
.
So what’s the right number? In 2023, total US goods exports were
$2,045 billion
, almost exactly ⅔ of all exports, including services.
How much of that involves blood? Well, the government keeps statistics on trade based on an insanely detailed
classification scheme
. All goods get some number. For example,
dirigibles
fall under
HTS 8801.90.0000
:
Leg warmers fall under HTS 6406.99.1530:
So what about blood? Well,
HTS 3002
is the category for:
Human blood; animal blood prepared for therapeutic, prophylactic or diagnostic uses; antisera and other blood fractions and modified immunological products, whether or not obtained by means of biotechnological processes; vaccines, toxins, cultures of micro-organisms (excluding yeasts) and similar products:
The total exports in this category in 2023 were 41.977 billion, or 2.05% of all goods exports. But that category includes many products that don’t require human blood such as most vaccines.
To get the actual data, you need to go through a
website
maintained by the US Trade Commission. This website has good and bad aspects. On the one hand, it’s slow and clunky and confusing and often randomly fails to deliver any results. On the other hand, when you re-submit, it clears your query and then blocks you for submitting too many requests, which is nice.
But after a lot of tearing of hair, I got what seems to be the most detailed breakdown of that category available. There are some finer subcategories in the taxonomy, but they don’t seem to have any data.
So let’s go through those categories. To start, here are some that would seem to almost always contain human blood:

data.title: Perfect Random Floating-Point Numbers
data.author: pclmulqdq
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了生成浮点随机数的常见方法及其缺陷，并介绍了一种新的解决方案。传统方法是生成一个随机整数，然后转换为浮点数并除以一个值，使其落在$$0, 1$$区间内。然而，这种方法无法访问该区间内的大多数浮点数，且最低有效位存在偏差，实际上是一种定点随机数生成器。新的方法解决了这些问题，能够在不显著影响性能的情况下生成“完美的”浮点随机数。文章还简要介绍了浮点数的结构、分布特性及四种浮点舍入模式，强调了生成浮点随机数时遵循舍入模式的重要性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：生成均匀随机浮点数的算法及其准确性、性能和实现复杂性

不同观点：
• camel-cdr 提出了一个生成均匀随机浮点数的算法，能够按比例覆盖所有可表示的浮点数值，但承认在处理次正规数（subnormal numbers）时存在轻微误差。该算法在准确性上优于常规算法，但性能较慢。
• FabHK 提到了另一种方法，即首先生成1到2之间的随机数，然后减去1，但指出这种方法仍然会错过一些可表示的数值。同时引用了Lemire和其他人的相关讨论，可能涉及更早的解决方案。
• possiblywrong 质疑了对生成器最低有效位存在偏差的观点，认为在特定情况下（如使用53位随机数）不会引入偏差。
• tialaramex 强调了不能生成真正的实数，实际需要的是生成二进制分数，并提出了一种基于随机位计数的实现方法。
• pixelpoet 提供了其他参考资料，认为文章中应提及这些资源。
• badmintonbaseba 指出将均匀随机浮点数从[0, 1)区间扩展到任意区间并不简单。
• FabHK 补充了一个有趣的事实，说明在不同浮点数区间内分布的浮点数比例差异巨大。
• hedora 希望文章能进一步探讨随机数测试，如Die Hard Battery。
• kevmo314 对文章中的解决方案表示赞赏，但希望其能更简单并被纳入语言的API中。
• gitroom 认为浮点数的非均匀分布特性使得简单方法不够理想，但理解追求全面覆盖的需求。
• sfpotter 提到了PRNGs的相关资源，并表示其在实践中效果良好。
• mahemm 质疑复杂算法是否比直接从/dev/urandom读取64位数据更有优势。
• lutusp 对“完美随机浮点数”的提法提出质疑，强调应说明“随机”实际上是“伪随机”。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于不同算法生成均匀随机浮点数的准确性和性能之间的权衡，以及实现复杂性是否值得。
• 各种方法在处理次正规数和不同浮点数区间时的表现也是讨论的重要内容。
• 引用的外部资源和相关文献为理解和实现这些算法提供了进一步的参考。

Perfect Random Floating-Point Numbers

When I recently looked at the state of the art in floating point random number generation,
I was surprised to see a common procedure in many programming languages and libraries that
is not really a floating-point algorithm:
Generate a random integer with bits chosen based on the precision of the format.
Convert to floating point.
Divide to produce an output between 0 and 1.
In code, this looks like:
1
func
(
r
*
Rand
)
Float64
()
float64
{
2
int64
rand_int
=
r
.
Int63n
(
1
<<
53
)
3
return
float64
(
rand_int
)
/
(
1
<<
53
)
4
}
This function is supposed to produce floating-point numbers drawn from a uniform distribution
in the interval $[0, 1)$. Zero is a possible output, but one is not, and the distribution is
uniform. The number "53" in the algorithm above is chosen in a way that is floating-point aware:
the double-precision floating-point numbers have 53 bits of precision, so this algorithm only
creates bits equal to the precision of the number system. It seems to fit the bill.
However, this algorithm has a few basic flaws. First, it cannot access most of the floating-point
numbers between 0 and 1. There are $2^{62}$
float64
numbers in this range, and this
algorithm can only access $2^{53}$ of them: $\frac{1}{512}$ of the space. Even if we had used a
larger integer range, like $2^{64}$, many random integers would alias to the same floating-point
result and some integers would round up to 1 during division. Second, the least significant bits
that come from this generator are biased.
This is really a
fixed-point
random number
generator followed by a conversion to floating point.
There have been some past attempts to fix these flaws, but none that avoid a huge
performance penalty while doing so. I recently finished a paper on a new method
for generating perfect random floating point numbers, and I have put a preprint on
Github
with a reference implementation in go. Thanks
to branch predictors, the perfect algorithm is not much slower than the fixed-point algorithm
above.
The Floating-Point Numbers Between 0 and 1
A floating-point number is a tuple of three components, packed into a 32- or 64-bit word:
Field
Meaning
Bits (
float32
)
Bits (
float64
)
Sign ($s$)
$+$ or $-$
1
1
Exponent ($e$)
Order of magnitude of the leading bit
8
11
Manitssa ($m$)
All significant bits after the leading bit
23
52
The storage of each number is efficient: the leading bit of the number is not stored since it can
be implied from the exponent as either being a zero (when $e = 0$, allowing $0$ to be represented)
or a one bit (all other cases). Floating point also has infinities and non-number values (NaN means
"not a number"), which are encoded with an exponent of all ones. Otherwise, the exponent is an
unsigned number that is stored so that subtraction of a bias can create a negative exponent. A
normal floating-point number has its value given by:
$$ F = (-1)^s 2^{e - eBias} (1.m) $$
Typically, $eBias$ is half of the representable range of the exponent field. The 32-bit floats
have an 8-bit exponent, and use $eBias = 127$, so the range of possible exponents is $-126$ to $127$
($e = 0$ and $e = 255$ have special meanings).
Half of all floating-point numbers lie between -1 and 1: every number with an exponent from $0$
up to $eBias$ is less than 1. This seems unintuitive, but it is an
artifact of how the floating-point numbers work: they have equal precision across the range of
magnitudes. The number $0.000001$ and the number $10^{20}$ both have 53 bits of precision (or 24
if we were using 32-bit floats). This is akin to the concept of "significant digits": every
floating-point number has 53 significant bits regardless of magnitude. The floating-point numbers
are power-law distributed, and many more of them have extreme magnitudes than it seems.
Floating-Point Rounding
When an operation produces too many bits, we need to round them to produce a floating-point result.
There are four floating-point rounding modes, but three are relatively specialized:
Round-to-nearest-ties-to-even
: Rounds to the nearest floating-point number, with ties going to
the even number. This is close to "rounding" as we learned in school except schoolbook rounding
involves ties going away from zero. Ties to even is better for numerical stability.
Round toward zero (truncation)
: Always round to the floating-point number closer to zero.
Equivalent to truncating trailing bits.
Round down
: Always round to the lower number.
Round up
: Always round to the higher number.
Nearest-ties-to-even is the default for arithmetic because it is the most accurate.
When we consider random number generation that is floating-point native, we may prefer to follow
the chosen rounding mode rather than using the strict idea of operating in $[0, 1)$. Number lines

data.title: Polycompiler: Merge Python and JavaScript code into one file that runs in both
data.author: nickoates
data.article_summary: Polycompiler 是一个实验性项目，旨在将 Python 和 JavaScript 代码合并到一个文件中，并根据运行环境执行对应代码。通过特殊语法，该文件在 Node.js 下执行 JavaScript 部分，在 Python 3 下执行 Python 部分。项目提供了 NPM 包，用户可以安装并使用命令行工具将 JS 和 Python 文件合并。输出文件使用 `.py.js` 扩展名，以确保 Node.js 能正确解析。该工具主要为趣味性而开发，也可能用于需要同时支持 Python 和 JS 用户的场景。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：多语言编程脚本的实现与扩展

不同观点：
• [mmastrac] 提出了一种不需要使用 `eval` 的多语言脚本技巧，通过巧妙利用多种语言的注释和字符串语法，实现同一个脚本文件可以在 Python 和 JavaScript 环境下运行。其论据包括：通过使用 Python 的多行字符串和 JavaScript 的块注释，可以分别让两段代码在各自的环境中运行。限制条件是 JavaScript 中不能包含 `"""`，Python 中不能包含 `*/`。

• [taraparo] 认为可以使用 Haxe 语言来编写代码，并通过 Haxe 的跨平台编译功能，将代码编译为多种语言（如 JavaScript, Python, C++, Java, Lua 等）。其论据是 Haxe 的跨平台特性可以避免在同一文件中混用不同语言语法，提供一种更规范的跨语言开发方式。

• [gobblik] 对 [mmastrac] 的方案表示赞赏，认为这种技巧很有趣，并提出希望这种方法可以进一步扩展，包含更多编程语言。虽然没有具体提出如何扩展，但表明了对多语言兼容性的兴趣。

• [GeekFortyTwo] 提出了一种更抽象的解决方案，建议使用一种元语言（如 FUT），通过编写一次代码并在多个引擎上运行。其观点倾向于通过更高层次的抽象和编译技术来解决多语言问题，而不是在同一个文件中混用不同语言的语法。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于 [mmastrac] 提出的方案虽然巧妙，但存在语法限制和可扩展性的问题。而 [taraparo] 和 [GeekFortyTwo] 提出的方案则更侧重于通过编译技术和元语言来实现更广泛的跨平台和跨语言支持。
• [gobblik] 对多语言兼容性的扩展需求表明，用户对这种多语言脚本的实际应用可能有更多期待，希望看到更广泛的适用性。

总结：讨论围绕如何实现多语言编程脚本展开，提出了具体的语法技巧、跨平台编译方案以及更高层次的元语言方案，并涉及可扩展性和实际应用场景的讨论。

An experimental project to attempt to merge arbitrary Python and JS code into one source file.
For example, the following code prints
Hello JS
when run with Node, and
Hello Python
when run with Python 3.
1
//
(
lambda
:
exec
(
"print('Hello Python')"
,
globals
())
or
1
)()
lambda
:
eval
(
"console.log('Hello JS')"
)
Installation & Use
Here's how you can get started with Polycompiler in a few simple steps.
Install
polycompiler
on NPM:
npm i polycompiler
Merge your files
Now, run the
polycompiler
command, providing the path to a JS file, a Python file, and an optional result file path.
When the output is run with Node.js
: It will run your JS file
When the output is run with Python
: It will run your Python file
polycompiler in.js in.py out.py.js
🚧 WIP
: The current file convention for Polycompiler output file extension is
.py.js
. This is becuase Node refuses to parse files of other file extensions, so it has to end in
js
.
Test it out
First, running it in Node should execute your JS
node out.py.js
And, running it with
python3
will execute the Python
python3 out.py.js
Why Polycompiler?
The best answer for this is honestly "for fun". However, it could also possibly be a possible solution for a single file that can be targeted to both Python and JS audiences (who may perhaps not have the other installed).
How does this work?
See my thought process in developing this
on YouTube
.
Let's work through this code to see how Polycompiler works:
1
//
(
lambda
:
exec
(
"print('Hello Python')"
,
globals
())
or
1
)()
lambda
:
eval
(
"console.log('Hello JS')"
)
Running the Output in Python
First, let's consider what happens when we run this in Python:
The first statement in of itself returns nothing, but the lambda function is executed, containing the
eval
with our target code
The second statement is not run at all, since the lambda expression is not called. Thus, the "incorrect" JS code in the
eval
is never run
This effectively only runs the Python code.
Running the Output in JS
Now, let's consider what happens if you run the code in JS. It's shown in a JS syntax-highlighted codeblock for clarity.
1
;
// (lambda: exec("print('Hello Python')", globals()) or 1)()
lambda:
eval
(
"console.log('Hello JS')"
)
;
The first statement, ignoring the JS comment, is simply an integer. It does nothing.
The second statement utilizes a clever trick with JS Labeled Statements: The
lambda:
at the start is treated as a label and is ignored. The eval is executed like normal and delivers the execution of the JS code in a string.
This effectively only runs the JavaScript code.
Summary
And just like that, we've managed to ignore the JS portion in Python and the Python portion in JS. Pretty neat!
While it seems simple in hindsight, this solution took a
long
time to figure out (even though some aspects of it are hiding in plain sight), so I hope it's interesting!

• [GeekFortyTwo] 提出了一种更抽象的解决方案，建议使用一种元语言（如 FUT），通过编写一次代码并在多个引擎上运行。其观点倾向于通过更高层次的抽象和编译技术来解决多语言问题，而不是在同一个文件中混用不同语言的语法。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于 [mmastrac] 提出的方案虽然巧妙，但存在语法限制和可扩展性的问题。而 [taraparo] 和 [GeekFortyTwo] 提出的方案则更侧重于通过编译技术和元语言来实现更广泛的跨平台和跨语言支持。
• [gobblik] 对多语言兼容性的扩展需求表明，用户对这种多语言脚本的实际应用可能有更多期待，希望看到更广泛的适用性。

总结：讨论围绕如何实现多语言编程脚本展开，提出了具体的语法技巧、跨平台编译方案以及更高层次的元语言方案，并涉及可扩展性和实际应用场景的讨论。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于Ozempic等减肥药物及其相关的商业、健康和生活方式影响的讨论。

不同观点：
• cmcaleer认为，Weight Watchers公司的问题源于13年前的高额债务，而不是Ozempic本身。Ozempic相关的业务调整只是为了挽救公司，但最终仍无法摆脱债务带来的负担。
• pmarreck分享了个人经历，指出使用Mounjaro减肥后，由于供应链和保险问题，体重反弹，且再次使用该药物效果不佳，提醒人们药物并非一劳永逸的解决方案。
• tlogan观察到GLP-1药物在减少酒精消费方面有显著效果，提供了药物使用的另一种视角。
• snapcaster对Ozempic持复杂态度，一方面为通过药物减肥的亲友感到高兴，另一方面担心这种解决方案可能导致更多人依赖制药行业，忽视生活方式的改变。
• codr7批评Weight Watchers可能制造了更多饮食失调问题，以增加回头客，质疑其商业模式。
• djd20不同意将Weight Watchers的失败归因于Ozempic，认为其失败是由于糟糕的客户体验和不断变化的计划。
• toomuchtodo强调了通过研究发现体重问题与激素和大脑化学物质的关系，提出过去在饮食和运动方面的努力可能被颠覆。
• ChildOfChaos认为Ozempic的高昂费用不值得，宁愿通过控制饮食来减肥，显示出对药物的怀疑态度。
• glp1guide提到Eli Lilly正在起诉配药商，并指出Semaglutide的专利即将部分到期，这可能影响未来药物的可及性。
• lanfeust6指出Ozempic和手术减肥都可能导致体重反弹，强调生活方式改变的必要性，认为药物只能作为短期工具，不能长期依赖。
• mrcwinn希望Weight Watchers在重组过程中能找到可持续的瘦身方法。
• damnesian警告长期使用人工诱导的减肥药物可能带来健康风险，主张通过自然方式减少摄入，强调生活方式调整的长远效益。

补充讨论：
• 评论中有多个个人经历和观察，提供了药物使用的实际效果和潜在问题。
• 关于Weight Watchers的商业困境，存在不同观点，有人认为是债务问题，有人则认为是客户体验和计划变动导致。
• 对Ozempic等药物的长期效果和依赖性存在广泛争议，部分人持乐观态度，而另一些人则担心其潜在风险和生活方式影响。
• 讨论还涉及到专利和法律问题，显示出药物市场竞争和可及性的复杂性。

争议焦点：
• Ozempic等药物是否能作为长期解决方案，或仅仅是短期工具。
• Weight Watchers公司问题的根本原因是债务还是客户体验和计划变动。
• 使用减肥药物是否会导致更多人依赖制药行业，忽视生活方式的改变。

data.title: Using tests as a debugging tool for logic errors
data.author: simplesort
data.article_summary: 本文主要讨论了Java开发中的逻辑错误及其调试方法，强调通过测试驱动的方式来隔离和解决这些错误。逻辑错误是指代码语法正确但业务逻辑不符合预期，例如计算折扣时未正确处理百分比。常见的逻辑错误包括差一错误（循环次数不正确）、操作顺序错误、类型混淆和边界条件疏忽等。传统调试方法往往难以发现和诊断这些错误，因此建议使用系统化的单元测试来定位和理解问题。文章介绍了几种调试技术，如假设测试（针对特定功能编写测试以验证假设）、状态推进测试和回归测试调试。有效的测试不仅能指出问题，还能提供上下文以帮助开发者找到正确的修复路径。文章还建议在设计测试时考虑调试需求，并探讨了使用AI辅助Java单元测试的可能性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：测试和逻辑错误在代码编写中的重要性及处理方法

不同观点：
• recroad认为文章过于复杂，本质上只是强调写测试。他质疑大多数开发者在开发算法时自然会写测试，尤其是在金融相关领域如税务计算。他还指出，文章没有深入讨论如何在运行时处理易错情况，并提到了Google的"error-prone"工具。

• jeremyscanvic引用Leslie Lamport的观点，强调确定代码要计算什么是更困难的部分，而不是如何编写代码。他以计算序列最大值为例，讨论了处理边缘情况的两种方法：返回错误或扩展数学定义。这种方法需要更多前期思考，但能简化代码和算法。

• pkoird提到在代码中使用断言（assertions）来检查前置条件、后置条件或不变量的做法，过去常被广泛使用，但在某些流行语言中已不再推荐。

• codr7简单提到页面字体有问题，未深入参与讨论。

• pfdietz关注如何通过变异测试（mutation testing）来验证测试是否能有效发现逻辑错误。他建议引入人为逻辑错误，观察测试是否能发现，并提出可以将变异作为测试生成器的一部分。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中提到了多种工具和方法，包括Google的"error-prone"工具和变异测试，这些工具和方法在发现和处理逻辑错误中可能具有重要作用。
• 不同观点之间的争议焦点在于如何有效编写和验证测试，以及在代码中处理边缘情况和逻辑错误的最佳实践。

data.title: Migrating a JavaScript Project from Prettier and ESLint to BiomeJS
data.author: unripe_syntax
data.article_summary: BiomeJS是一款新兴的JavaScript工具，旨在替代Prettier和ESLint，通过集成代码格式化和代码检查功能，简化工作流并提升性能。它源自于已终止的Rome项目，但已发展成独立的工具链，使用Rust编写，具备多线程能力，速度比Prettier快25倍，比ESLint快15倍。Biome的格式化功能与Prettier类似，但语言支持较少；其代码检查功能受ESLint启发，支持自定义规则和多语言。安装和使用简单，通过NPM分发，无需配置文件即可开始使用。Biome通过`format`和`lint`命令分别进行代码格式化和检查，并提供详细的错误和警告信息。是否从Prettier和ESLint迁移到Biome，取决于项目需求和语言支持情况。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Rome/Biome、Prettier和ESLint等前端开发工具的讨论，涉及工具的性能、实用性、生态支持以及迁移过程中的问题。

不同观点：
• **对Rome/Biome的批评与反思**：
  - [jemmyw] 认为Rome在实际工具发布前就获得了大量关注和讨论，但最终没有实现承诺。这种现象类似于一些过度炒作但最终失败的公司。作者对Rome背后的驱动因素感到困惑，质疑其目的和吸引力。
  - [egorfine] 提到前端开发工具的快速变化和对生态系统的不信任感，指出Rome的消亡是其中一个例子。作者引用了“红皇后的赛跑”来比喻前端开发需要不断奔跑才能保持在原地。

• **对Prettier和ESLint的肯定与依赖**：
  - [mrbluecoat] 表示虽然Biome声称能合并工具节省时间，但实际影响微乎其微，自己只需要每三年在VSCode中点击一次。
  - [progx] 提到虽然Biome有性能优势，但在需要自定义时还是会回到Prettier，认为性能并不是真正的问题。
  - [zoogeny] 经过分析后选择了Prettier和ESLint，认为Biome仍在追赶中，稳定性不足。
  - [DGCA] 和团队成员都不喜欢Biome，迁移回Prettier和ESLint后发现了很多之前未报告的问题。

• **对Biome的有限支持与迁移挑战**：
  - [exiguus] 分享了迁移到Biome的经验，指出在TypeScript项目中效果不错，但在React和Angular项目中遇到性能问题。迁移整个公司代码规范到Biome几乎不可能，因为依赖许多ESLint插件。
  - [sibeliius] 也遇到了类似问题，Biome在处理嵌入式语言（如GraphQL）时不够完善，最终回到了Prettier。

• **对工具生态和开发体验的讨论**：
  - [horsawlarway] 认为文章更像是营销材料，缺乏实际迁移过程中的成本、问题和收益分析。
  - [difosfor] 提到Biome缺少许多ESLint插件支持，最终只能结合使用。
  - [herpdyderp] 对Prettier的插件系统不满，认为其存在持续的bug且难以编写插件。

• **对工具未来发展的期待**：
  - [Alifatisk] 和[jmisavage] 对Biome的统一工具链理念表示兴趣，询问是否有实际使用经验和收益。
  - [7bit] 对Prettier的HTML格式化问题表示不满，期待其他替代方案。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于Rome/Biome是否能够真正替代Prettier和ESLint，特别是在大型项目中的实用性和稳定性。
- 讨论中多次提到工具的性能优势与实际需求之间的差距，许多开发者认为现有工具已经足够快，性能并不是主要问题。
- 另一个值得注意的点是前端开发工具的生态系统和插件支持，许多开发者在迁移过程中遇到了插件兼容性问题，这成为了Biome等新工具推广的主要障碍。

43913950.article_content:
Prettier and ESLint have long been indispensable tools in the JavaScript
ecosystem for ensuring code consistency and quality. They have become
staples in the toolchains of JavaScript projects worldwide.
However, a new player has emerged to challenge their dominance:
BiomeJS. This ambitious project seeks to combine the
functionality of both tools into a single, high-performance solution for code
formatting and linting.
By combining these capabilities, Biome aims to simplify workflows, reduce
configuration complexity, and significantly boost performance, thus positioning
itself as the next generation of JavaScript tooling.
In this article, I'll introduce the BiomeJS project, explore its setup, and help
you decide if migrating from Prettier and ESLint is the right move for you.
What Is Biome?
BiomeJS
started its life as a fork of the now-defunct
Rome project
, but has since evolved into its
own distinct toolchain focused on providing a fast, integrated development
experience.
It currently provides two solutions for JavaScript developers:
A Prettier-like code formatter.
A powerful linter that's inspired by ESLint.
By combining these tools into a single solution, Biome minimizes the need for
multiple configurations, thus creating a more seamless experience for
developers.
It is also built with a modern architecture, using Rust for speed and
multi-threading, making it more than an order of magnitude faster than its
predecessors.
In this way, it represents not only a replacement but also a significant leap
forward in simplifying and optimizing the JavaScript development workflow.
Comparison with Prettier
Biome's formatter, like Prettier's, offers only a few configuration options. Its
output is mostly compatible with Prettier — though there are some
differences
— and
it formats about
25 times faster
because it's multithreaded and written in Rust.
While
Biome supports multiple languages
,
it lags behind Prettier in terms of coverage. Notably, HTML, Markdown, and SCSS
are not yet supported, and frameworks like Vue, Astro, and Svelte have only
partial support.
Comparison with ESLint for JavaScript
Many of Biome's linting rules are inspired by ESLint and other popular linters,
and organized into specific categories. Like ESLint, these rules are fully
configurable, allowing you to disable any rule or enable only a subset.
You can customize how rule violations are handled, choosing whether they trigger
warnings or errors, and whether automatic fixes should be suggested. For
example:
JSON
{
"linter"
: {
"rules"
: {
"correctness"
: {
"noUnusedVariables"
: {
"level"
:
"error"
,
"fix"
:
"none"
}
},
"style"
: {
"useConst"
: {
"level"
:
"warn"
,
"fix"
:
"unsafe"
}
}
}
}
}
Biome's linter also extends beyond JavaScript/TypeScript by supporting other
languages. It includes several CSS linting rules from
stylelint-config-recommended
with more in development. For a full list of supported rules, refer to the
Biome documentation
.
In terms of performance,
Biome is over 15 times faster than ESLint
,
again thanks to its Rust-based, multi-threaded architecture.
Getting Started with Biome
Although Biome isn't written in JavaScript, its executable is distributed
through the
NPM registry
, so you
can easily install it through your preferred package manager:
Shell
npm

data.title: Sandy Bridge-era motherboard gets M.2 SSD boot support 12 years after launch
data.author: mobilio
data.article_summary: Gigabyte发布了针对B75M-D3H主板的固件更新（F16f），主要用于修复2024年发现的PKfail漏洞。尽管该主板早在2012年推出，且已超出其生命周期，但新固件意外地增加了对从NVMe SSD（如M.2 SSD）启动的支持。这一功能原本是不支持的，因为主板仅有SATA接口。通过使用M.2到PCIe适配器，用户可以在老旧的B75M-D3H上利用NVMe驱动器，尽管在PCIe 2.0接口下性能有所降低。目前尚不清楚这一支持是无意中加入还是有意为之，但此举可能为其他老主板带来了类似功能。

• [rfv6723] 认为可以通过USB驱动器上的引导加载程序启动NVMe驱动器上的操作系统，并提到使用CloverBootloader的多年经验，提供了一个开源链接。

43914677.article_content:
(Image credit: Gigabyte)
Firmware updates for motherboards aim to fix bugs and occasionally introduce new features. However,
Chinese netizen
WhiteCamellia (via
Uniko's Hardware
) found that manufacturers often fail to promote these new features. Notably, Gigabyte has seemingly updated the 13-year-old B75M-D3H motherboard to support booting from NVMe SSDs, like M.2 SSDs, a previously unavailable functionality.
Introduced in 2012, the B75M-D3H is a motherboard featuring the B75 chipset, designed to support Intel's 2nd Generation (
Sandy Bridge
) and 3rd Generation (
Ivy Bridge
) Core processors. Clearly, the motherboard is beyond its end-of-life (EOL) status.
Ancient but not forgotten, Gigabyte issued a new firmware (F16f) for the B75M-D3H motherboard in 2024 to address the
PKfail vulnerability
discovered in the same year. The update is particularly noteworthy, as the last firmware update (F15) received by the B75M-D3H was in 2013, over ten years prior. The F16f firmware primarily addresses the PKfail issue. However, WhiteCamellia identified an additional functionality. An analysis of the F16f firmware using UEFITool reveals the inclusion of the NVMe DXE trifecta (Nvme, NvmeSmm, NVMEINT13), which is essential for booting from NVMe drives, like M.2.
The B75M-D3H was not designed to accommodate NVMe SSDs. The motherboard features one SATA III and five SATA II connectors for storage, explaining its initial lack of support for booting from NVMe drives. Nonetheless, users can employ M.2 to PCIe adapters, allowing M.2 drives to connect with the motherboard via its expansion ports. That is precisely the approach WhiteCamellia took to use his
Western Digital WD SN740
with the B75M-D3H motherboard.
The SN740 is a PCIe 4.0 x4 SSD that provides sequential read and write speeds of up to 2,000 MB/s. When installed on a slower interface, it logically results in reduced performance. On the B75M-D3H motherboard, the SN740 operates at PCIe 2.0 x4 speeds. This limitation is not due to the motherboard itself, as the B75M-D3H has a fully functional PCIe 3.0 x16 expansion slot. However, when paired with a
Sandy Bridge
processor, that slot operates at PCIe 2.0 speeds, which we suspect is the case with WhiteCamellia.
PCIe 2.0 storage speeds may seem underwhelming in modern times, considering PCIe 5.0 drives have
been around for a couple of years now
. However, the transition from SATA III to PCIe 2.0 is quite substantial and could revive aging systems to bring some snappiness to the operating system and everyday applications.
For quite some time, enthusiasts have modified firmware to enable unsupported processors or SSDs to function with newer motherboards. Regarding the B75M-D3H, it's unclear whether Gigabyte intentionally or unintentionally provided NVMe boot support. The PKfail vulnerability impacts numerous Intel platforms, covering the 60-series to 100-series chipsets, all of which received firmware updates from Gigabyte in September 2024. It's possible that this new firmware introduced similar functionality to other older motherboards aside from the B75M-D3H.

data.title: Optimizing Common Lisp
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何使用SBCL内置的统计性能分析工具**sb-sprof**来优化Common Lisp代码，重点分析CPU和内存分配的瓶颈。作者通过分析**parcom/json**模块，成功将运行速度提升了3倍，并将内存分配减少了25倍。文章详细说明了如何使用`with-profiling`宏在CPU模式和内存模式下进行性能分析，识别出如`consume`等热点函数。通过优化技术，如避免不必要的工作、使用`simple-string`和`schar`、多返回值、栈分配和Lambda缓存，有效提升了性能。最终，作者强调了数据驱动优化决策的重要性，而不是仅凭猜测进行优化。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对Common Lisp（CL）代码优化的不同观点和工具使用建议

不同观点：
• [metroholografix] 认为新手在CL代码中经常使用 `(optimize (speed 3) (safety 0))` 是一种不好的习惯，虽然可以提高速度，但会牺牲安全性，例如去掉数组边界检查和类型检查。他建议使用 `(optimize (speed 3) (safety 1))`，认为这样在大多数情况下能保持相近的性能，同时保留必要的安全检查。此外，他还推荐了SBCL中的sb-simd库，以及通过编译器宏和VM内部钩子进行自定义代码生成的方法。

• [dom2] 补充了关于性能分析工具的具体使用建议，指出在使用 `sb-sprof` 进行性能分析后，可以调用 `(disassemble '<profiled function>)` 来查看增强的汇编代码，并显示每个指令的采样命中比例，这有助于进一步优化代码。

• [mark_l_watson] 对上述内容表示感谢，并提到自己曾在LispWorks Pro中进行过性能分析，但尚未在SBCL中尝试。他还顺便提到了对metroholografix提到的烹饪页面的赞赏。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：[metroholografix] 明确反对新手过度优化代码时牺牲安全性，认为 `(optimize (speed 3) (safety 0))` 是一种坏习惯。虽然没有直接的反对意见，但[mark_l_watson] 和 [dom2] 的回复更侧重于工具使用和实践经验，没有直接回应此观点。

• 工具和实践：讨论中提到了多个具体的工具和库，如 `sb-simd`、`sb-sprof` 和 `(disassemble ...)`，这些工具可以帮助开发者更好地进行性能分析和优化。

• 实际操作建议：[metroholografix] 提供了具体的优化建议和替代方案，[dom2] 则补充了性能分析后如何查看汇编代码的具体操作步骤，提供了实用性的指导。

43913727.article_content:
Table of Contents
Introduction to sb-sprof
time
with-profiling: CPU Mode
with-profiling: Memory Mode
Optimization Techniques
Avoiding Work
simple-string and schar
Multiple Return Values
Stack Allocation
Lambda Caching
Conclusion
Optimizing Common Lisp
By Colin on 2025-05-07
I recently released a
Parser Combinator library
for Common Lisp, but was unhappy with its performance. This article is a description of how I used
sb-sprof
, built in to SBCL, to identify both CPU and memory allocation hotspots, improving the runtime speed of the
parcom/json
module by 3x and decreasing memory allocation by 25x.
Introduction to sb-sprof
SBCL has a number of built-in extension libraries.
sb-sprof
is a "statistical profiler" that periodically samples the call stack to see where time is being spent and who is doing the most allocating. In my
parcom/benchmarks
system, I have:
(require :sb-sprof)
;; OVERALL
(let ((s (uiop:read-file-string "tests/data/large-file.json")))
(time (pj:parse s)))
;; SPEED
(let ((s (uiop:read-file-string "tests/data/large-file.json")))
(sb-sprof:with-profiling (:max-samples 100000 :sample-interval 0.00001 :report :graph)
(aref (pj:parse s) 0)))
;; MEMORY
(let ((s (uiop:read-file-string "tests/data/large-file.json")))
(sb-sprof:with-profiling (:max-samples 100000 :sample-interval 0.00001 :report :graph :mode :alloc)
(aref (pj:parse s) 0)))
Like
time
, just by wrapping a call with
with-profiling
we can interactively profile any function we wish.
time
time
itself is available in any CL implementation and is a quick way to gauge the overall performance of something. Running the
OVERALL
form above, we see:
Evaluation took:
0.881 seconds of real time
0.877017 seconds of total run time (0.867189 user, 0.009828 system)
[ Real times consist of 0.079 seconds GC time, and 0.802 seconds non-GC time. ]
[ Run times consist of 0.078 seconds GC time, and 0.800 seconds non-GC time. ]
99.55% CPU
2,474,196,347 processor cycles
261,309,152 bytes consed
Before I started optimizing,
time
was reporting 6.5 billion bytes consed, which is where the "25x reduction" stat comes from.
with-profiling: CPU Mode
Evaluting the
SPEED
form above, we see:
Self        Total        Cumul
Nr  Count     %  Count     %  Count     %    Calls  Function
------------------------------------------------------------------------
1    159  19.4    270  33.0    159  19.4        -  (LAMBDA (PC::OFFSET) :IN PC:CONSUME)
2     73   8.9     73   8.9    232  28.3        -  SB-KERNEL:TWO-ARG->=
3     63   7.7     67   8.2    295  36.0        -  PJ::ESCAPED
4     55   6.7     55   6.7    350  42.7        -  (LAMBDA (PJ::C) :IN PJ:STRING)
5     39   4.8     45   5.5    389  47.5        -  (LAMBDA (PC::OFFSET) :IN PC:CHAR)
6     38   4.6     76   9.3    427  52.1        -  PC:CHAR
7     37   4.5     37   4.5    464  56.7        -  SB-IMPL::GETHASH/EQL-HASH
8     33   4.0     48   5.9    497  60.7        -  PC:CONSUME
9     27   3.3     27   3.3    524  64.0        -  SB-IMPL::GETHASH/EQ-HASH/FLAT
10     18   2.2    405  49.5    542  66.2        -  PJ:STRING
...
And so on. Perhaps the most relevant column here is
Self %
, which tells us how much of the total runtime was spent inside the named function. In this case we see it spending the most time within the innards of the
consume
parser. "Data ends arguments" as they say, so it is helpful to know where the time is actually being spent as opposed to guessing. Here, it wouldn't make sense for me to optimize
string
(only 2% of the total) when
consume
is so clearly a hotspot.
Normally the
:report
mode is
:flat
, but by setting it to
:graph
we are shown where each function is called from, and what it calls:
Callers
Total.     Function
Count     %  Count     %      Callees
------------------------------------------------------------------------
3   0.4                   (LAMBDA (PC::OFFSET) :IN PC:CONSUME) [1]
35   4.3                   PJ::SKIP-SPACE [17]
1   0.1                   (LAMBDA (#:*>-OFFSET2) :IN PC:BETWEEN) [11]
159  19.4    270  33.0   (LAMBDA (PC::OFFSET) :IN PC:CONSUME) [1]
1   0.1                   PC:CONSUME [8]
3   0.4                   (LAMBDA (PC::OFFSET) :IN PC:CONSUME) [1]
4   0.5                   PC::OFF [23]
6   0.7                   PC:SPACE? [22]
50   6.1                   (LAMBDA (PJ::C) :IN PJ:STRING) [4]
47   5.7                   SB-KERNEL:TWO-ARG->= [2]
------------------------------------------------------------------------
...
And so on. Here it looks like it's often being used to skip over whitespace.
with-profiling: Memory Mode

:mode :alloc
, the output of
with-profiling
becomes memory-focused.
Self        Total        Cumul
Nr  Count     %  Count     %  Count     %    Calls  Function
------------------------------------------------------------------------
1   6282  74.3   6282  74.3   6282  74.3        -  ALLOC-TRAMP
2   1177  13.9   1177  13.9   7459  88.3        -  SYS-ALLOC-TRAMP

43913727.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何使用SBCL内置的统计性能分析工具**sb-sprof**来优化Common Lisp代码，重点分析CPU和内存分配的瓶颈。作者通过分析**parcom/json**模块，成功将运行速度提升了3倍，并将内存分配减少了25倍。文章详细说明了如何使用`with-profiling`宏在CPU模式和内存模式下进行性能分析，识别出如`consume`等热点函数。通过优化技术，如避免不必要的工作、使用`simple-string`和`schar`、多返回值、栈分配和Lambda缓存，有效提升了性能。最终，作者强调了数据驱动优化决策的重要性，而不是仅凭猜测进行优化。
43913727.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对Common Lisp（CL）代码优化的不同观点和工具使用建议

不同观点：
• [metroholografix] 认为新手在CL代码中经常使用 `(optimize (speed 3) (safety 0))` 是一种不好的习惯，虽然可以提高速度，但会牺牲安全性，例如去掉数组边界检查和类型检查。他建议使用 `(optimize (speed 3) (safety 1))`，认为这样在大多数情况下能保持相近的性能，同时保留必要的安全检查。此外，他还推荐了SBCL中的sb-simd库，以及通过编译器宏和VM内部钩子进行自定义代码生成的方法。

• [dom2] 补充了关于性能分析工具的具体使用建议，指出在使用 `sb-sprof` 进行性能分析后，可以调用 `(disassemble '<profiled function>)` 来查看增强的汇编代码，并显示每个指令的采样命中比例，这有助于进一步优化代码。

• [mark_l_watson] 对上述内容表示感谢，并提到自己曾在LispWorks Pro中进行过性能分析，但尚未在SBCL中尝试。他还顺便提到了对metroholografix提到的烹饪页面的赞赏。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：[metroholografix] 明确反对新手过度优化代码时牺牲安全性，认为 `(optimize (speed 3) (safety 0))` 是一种坏习惯。虽然没有直接的反对意见，但[mark_l_watson] 和 [dom2] 的回复更侧重于工具使用和实践经验，没有直接回应此观点。

• 工具和实践：讨论中提到了多个具体的工具和库，如 `sb-simd`、`sb-sprof` 和 `(disassemble ...)`，这些工具可以帮助开发者更好地进行性能分析和优化。

• 实际操作建议：[metroholografix] 提供了具体的优化建议和替代方案，[dom2] 则补充了性能分析后如何查看汇编代码的具体操作步骤，提供了实用性的指导。

data.author: arathore
data.article_summary: "ty" 是一个用 Rust 编写的高性能 Python 类型检查器和语言服务器。该项目仍在开发中，尚未达到生产可用阶段。贡献者可以通过在项目仓库中提交 issue 来反馈问题或参与开发，而拉取请求则应提交到 Ruff 仓库。项目采用 MIT 许可证，贡献代码即视为同意该许可条款。当前，项目包含 325 个星标和 3 个分支，主要使用 Python、Dockerfile 和 Shell 编写。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Astral推出的预发布软件"ty"及其相关工具的评价与讨论

不同观点：
• 对Astral及其新工具的积极期待：
  - [zanie] 强调"ty"目前处于预alpha阶段，版本为0.0.0a6，旨在验证发布流程，并表示未来将有更多更新。
  - [Handprint4469] 提供了如何在不安装情况下测试"ty"的建议。
  - [rexledesma] 表示对Astral新推出的Python语言服务器的期待，尤其是在Pylance不兼容的情况下。
  - [tiltowait] 分享了在个人项目中使用"ty"的积极体验，速度显著快于pyright。

• 对Astral工具速度和性能的讨论：
  - [tmvphil] 比较了"ty"和mypy在一个大项目上的检查时间，"ty"仅用0.5秒，而mypy需要18秒。
  - [throwaway63467] 认为用Rust编写类型检查器是提高速度的明显选择，因为mypy速度较慢。

• 对Astral工具兼容性和实用性的关注：
  - [aleksanb] 指出目前类型检查器对现实中Python代码的丰富性支持不足，特别是对Django的支持，并希望更多工具采用类似TypeScript的全面方法。
  - [cristea] 直接询问"ty"是否支持Django stubs，因为这是其公司切换类型检查器的障碍。

• 对Astral商业模式的疑问：
  - [krupan] 和 [cyounkins] 都提到了Astral如何盈利的问题，显示出对该公司商业模式的关注。

• 对Python工具整体生态的评价：
  - [blibble] 对比了Python工具与Java工具的历史和现状，认为Astral的出现极大地改善了Python工具链。
  - [ngoldbaum] 提到将"ty"项目名称转让给Astral，并提及Astral对Python软件基金会的捐赠，显示出对Astral贡献的认可。

补充讨论：
• [nickagliano] 提到Facebook也推出了类似的Python类型检查器Pyrefly，并指出Rust在Python和JS工具领域的影响力不断增强。
• [pizza] 建议"ty"在初期阶段能够支持t-string，以便在不执行代码的情况下提供可靠的检查功能。

争议焦点：
• 对类型检查器在支持现实Python代码（特别是Django）方面的能力存在争议，部分用户希望工具能更全面地涵盖各种实际使用情况。

总结：
Astral的新工具"ty"引起了广泛关注，用户对其速度和潜力表示期待，但对其兼容性和商业模式仍有疑问。同时，Rust在Python工具领域的崛起也成为讨论的热点。

data.title: Show HN: eInk optimized manga with Kindle Comic Converter (+Kobo/ReMarkable)
data.author: seam_carver
data.article_summary: Kindle Comic Converter (KCC) 是一款将漫画和漫画转换为电子书格式的工具，专为eink阅读器（如Kindle、Kobo、ReMarkable等）优化。它支持全屏无边界显示，并针对固定布局进行优化，特别适合eink屏幕的显示需求。KCC提供多种图像处理选项，并可根据设备屏幕分辨率缩放以优化文件大小和性能。支持的输入格式包括文件夹、CBZ、CBR、PDF等，输出格式包括MOBI、AZW3、EPUB、KEPUB和CBZ。该工具还提供了命令行版本和多种安装方式（如Windows、Mac、Docker等），并附有详细的使用说明和常见问题解答。KCC并非亚马逊官方工具，专为漫画/漫画读者设计，而非出版商。

KCC
Kindle Comic Converter
optimizes comics and manga for eink readers like Kindle, Kobo, ReMarkable, and more.
Pages display in fullscreen without margins, with proper fixed layout support.
Its main feature is various optional image processing steps to look good on eink screens,
which have different requirements than normal LCD screens.
It also does filesize optimization by downscaling to your specific device's screen resolution,
which can improve performance on underpowered ereaders.
Supported input formats include folders/CBZ/CBR/PDF of JPG/PNG files and more.
Supported output formats include virtual panel view MOBI/AZW3, EPUB, KEPUB, and CBZ.
YouTube tutorial (please subscribe):
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IR2Fhcm9658

is not

Amazon's tool is for comic publishers and involves a lot of manual effort, while
KCC

in no way is a replacement for
KCC

data.title: Waiting for Postgres 18: Accelerating Disk Reads with Asynchronous I/O
data.author: lfittl
data.article_summary:
Postgres 18引入异步I/O（AIO），显著改变了I/O处理方式，尤其在云环境中能大幅提升性能。异步I/O允许并发处理多个读请求，无需等待每个请求完成，从而减少I/O等待时间。Postgres 17通过引入读流API为异步I/O打下基础，但仍依赖操作系统内核的预读取机制。Postgres 18则直接由数据库获取数据，绕过内核机制，提高I/O效率。

Postgres 18新增了`io_method`配置参数，控制I/O操作方式，包括：
1. `io_method = sync`：保持同步I/O模式。
2. `io_method = worker`：使用后台I/O工作进程处理读请求，不阻塞主进程。
3. `io_method = io_uring`：利用Linux的io_uring实现高效异步I/O。

在AWS上的测试显示，异步I/O使读取性能翻倍，io_uring表现尤为突出。当前版本AIO仅支持读操作，写操作仍为同步。用户需根据实际环境调整`io_method`和`effective_io_concurrency`以优化性能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Postgres项目的影响力、技术细节（如异步I/O、性能优化）、与MySQL/MariaDB等数据库的对比、生产环境中的实际应用以及安全问题。

不同观点：
• Postgres的贡献者和社区受到高度评价，有人认为它是继Linux之后对商业技术世界影响最大的开源项目（drdrek）。
• 有人关注Linux中的preadv2(..., RWF_NOWAIT)用于非阻塞读取，以减少延迟（the8472）。
• 关于异步I/O功能是否仅限于Linux，有评论指出Windows也有IORing实现，并提供了比较文章链接（nu11ptr）。
• FreeBSD的aio(4)也被认为值得关注，因其没有Linux/glibc aio的缺点（kev009）。

补充讨论：
• Postgres与MySQL的历史对比，有人提到Postgres最终胜出（rks404）。
• 有人将Postgres的异步I/O方法与MySQL的InnoDB进行比较（skeptrune）。
• 生产环境中使用Postgres的实际案例，包括在NVMe上的性能优势（shayonj）和在Hetzner服务器上的具体优化措施（niux）。
• 关于云服务与本地硬件的性能和价格对比，有人指出云服务在性能上相对落后但价格高昂（martinald）。
• 对io_uring安全问题的关注，有人提到因安全问题而被禁用的情况（p_ing）。

• 云服务与本地硬件在性能和价格上的巨大差异，以及对异步I/O在不同硬件环境中的重要性的不同看法（martinald）。
• 异步I/O功能在不同操作系统上的实现和安全问题（nu11ptr, p_ing）。

Postgres shouldn’t feel like a black box:
Watch our product webinar
to see the latest features.
Waiting for Postgres 18: Accelerating Disk Reads with Asynchronous I/O
By
Lukas Fittl
May 07, 2025
With the Postgres 18 Beta 1 release this week a multi-year effort, and significant architectural shift in Postgres is taking shape:
Asynchronous I/O (AIO)
. These capabilities are still under active development, but they represent a fundamental change in how Postgres handles I/O, offering the potential for significant performance gains, particularly in cloud environments where latency is often the bottleneck.
Why asynchronous I/O matters
How Postgres 17’s read streams paved the way
New io_method setting in Postgres 18
io_method = sync
io_method = worker
io_method = io_uring
Asynchronous I/O in action
Benchmark on AWS: Doubling read performance & even greater gains from io_uring
Tuning effective_io_concurrency
Monitoring I/Os in flight with pg_aios
Heads Up: Async I/O makes I/O timing information hard to interpret
Conclusion
In summary
References
While some features may still be adjusted or dropped during the beta period before the final release, now is the best time to test and validate how Postgres 18 performs in practice. In Postgres 18 AIO is limited to read operations; writes remain synchronous, though support may expand in future versions.
In this post, we explain what asynchronous I/O is, how it works in Postgres 18, and what it means for performance optimization.
Why asynchronous I/O matters
Postgres has historically operated under a synchronous I/O model, meaning every read request is a blocking system call. The database must pause and wait for the operating system to return the data before continuing. This design introduces unnecessary waits on I/O, especially in cloud environments where storage is often network-attached (e.g. Amazon EBS) and I/O can have over 1ms of latency.
In a simplified model, we can illustrate the difference like this, ignoring any prefetching/batching the Linux kernel might do:
You can picture synchronous I/O like an imaginary librarian who retrieves one book at a time, returning before fetching the next. This inefficiency compounds as the number of physical reads for a logical operation increases.
Asynchronous I/O eliminates that bottleneck by allowing programs to issue multiple read requests concurrently, without waiting for prior reads to return. In an async program flow, I/O requests are scheduled to be read into a memory location and the program waits for completion of those reads, instead of issuing each read individually.
How Postgres 17’s read streams paved the way
The work for implementing asynchronous I/O in Postgres has been many years in the making. Postgres 17 introduced an essential internal abstration,
with the introduction of read stream APIs
. These internal changes standardized how read operations were issued across different subsystems and streamlined the use of
posix_fadvise()
to request that the operating system prefetch data in advance.
However, this advisory mechanism only hinted to the kernel to load data into the OS page cache, not into Postgres’ own shared buffers. Postgres still had to issue syscalls for each read, and OS readahead behaviour is not always consistent.
The upcoming Postgres 18 release removes this indirection. With true asynchronous reads, data is fetched directly into shared buffers by the database itself, bypassing reliance on kernel-level heuristics and enabling more predictable, higher-throughput I/O behavior.
New io_method setting in Postgres 18
To control the mechanism used for asynchronous I/O, Postgres 18 introduces a new configuration parameter:
io_method
. This setting determines how read operations are dispatched under the hood, and whether they’re handled synchronously, offloaded to I/O workers, or submitted directly to the kernel via
io_uring
.
The
io_method
setting must be set in postgresql.conf and cannot be changed without restarting. It controls which  I/O implementation Postgres will use and is essential to understand when tuning I/O performance in Postgres 18. There are three possible settings for io_method, with the current default (as of Beta 1) being
worker
.
io_method = sync
The
sync
setting in Postgres 18 mirrors the synchronous behavior as was implemented in Postgres 17. Reads are still synchronous and blocking, using
posix_fadvise()
to achieve read-ahead in the Linux kernel.
io_method = worker
The
worker
setting utilizes dedicated
I/O worker processes
running in the background that retrieve data independently of query execution. The main backend process enqueues read requests, and these workers interact with the Linux kernel to fetch data, which is then delivered into shared buffers,
without blocking the main process
.
The number of I/O workers can be configured through the new
io_workers
setting, and defaults to
3
. These workers are always running, and shared across all connections and databases.
io_method = io_uri

data.title: Create and edit images with Gemini 2.0 in preview
data.author: meetpateltech
data.article_summary: Google宣布在其AI开发平台Google AI Studio和Vertex AI中推出Gemini 2.0 Flash的图像生成预览功能。开发者现在可以使用Gemini API集成对话式图像生成与编辑，新版本在视觉质量、文字渲染和过滤器拦截率方面有显著改进。主要功能包括在不同环境中重新定位产品、实时协作编辑图像、对话式编辑图像特定部分、动态创建新产品SKU等。开发者可以通过Gemini Co-Drawing Sample App体验这些功能，并使用指定模型名在API中开始构建。Google计划未来进一步提升质量和扩展功能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Gemini 2.0多模态图像生成模型的性能、使用体验及其应用场景

不同观点：
• **vunderba**：将Gemini 2.0与OpenAI 4o、Midjourney 7、Flux等顶尖图像生成模型进行了对比，认为Gemini 2.0在美学质量上不如Google之前的Imagen 3.0。不过，Gemini 2.0在多模态支持和生成速度上优于OpenAI 4o。
• **eminence32**：对使用对话界面进行图像生成的效果表示怀疑，认为描述复杂图像的词汇有限，调整生成结果的过程较为困难，可能需要更多的想象力。
• **simonw**：指出使用Gemini 2.0生成图像的成本较高，41MB的JSON包含28张图片，成本超过1美元，并提供了一个工具来渲染生成的JSON数据。
• **Tsarp**：认为直接测试和结合工具（如controlnets）测试的结果可能会有很大差异，开放模型如Flux通过适当工具可以生成更高质量的图像。
• **mkl**：对Gemini 2.0在生成图像细节上的表现提出质疑，认为在处理复杂指令时结果不如预期。
• **cush**：对Gemini的涂鸦演示感到有趣，并分享了相关链接。
• **emporas**：分享了使用Gemini生成专辑封面的复杂工作流程，结合了其他LLM模型以优化结果。
• **Yiling-J**：展示了使用Gemini 2.0生成100个食谱及其图像的成果，认为结果良好，并分享了开源项目链接。
• **minimaxir**：指出Gemini 2.0每张图片的定价为0.039美元，高于Imagen 3的0.03美元，并讨论了Gemini 2.0在对话生成图像上的优势和Imagen 3在图像质量上的可能优势。
• **mNovak**：对Gemini 2.0的共同绘图演示结果不一，特别是在理解火柴人图示方面存在问题。
• **thornewolf**：认为Gemini 2.0的输出结果不错，但仍有较多失败情况，期待更多已知良好工作流的展示。
• **pentagrama**：反思Gemini 2.0的应用可能指向电商和购物场景，担心AI生成内容泛滥对人类工艺和真实物品的冲击。
• **egamirorrim**：对如何使用Gemini 2.0编辑照片感到困惑，尝试修改图片但结果与原图差异较大。
• **qq99**：质疑Gemini 2.0的新功能是否已经在AI Studio中提供，并认为新版本的改进难以追踪。

补充讨论：
• **成本与定价**：simonw和minimaxir提到了Gemini 2.0的使用成本较高，并与Imagen 3进行了对比。
• **生成图像的质量与细节处理**：vunderba、mkl和mNovak对Gemini 2.0在处理复杂指令和生成高质量图像上的表现提出了质疑。
• **应用场景与潜在影响**：emporas和pentagrama讨论了Gemini 2.0在专辑封面制作和电商场景中的应用，并反思了AI生成内容对人类工艺的潜在影响。
• **工具与工作流**：Tsarp和emporas分享了结合其他工具和LLM模型优化图像生成结果的经验。

争议焦点：
• Gemini 2.0在图像生成质量、成本和应用场景上的表现和价值存在争议，部分用户认为其生成质量和细节处理不如其他模型，而部分用户则对其多模态支持和速度表示赞赏。
