The US Senate today voted along party lines to kill a Federal Communications Commission program to distribute Wi-Fi hotspots to schoolchildren, with Democrats saying the Republican-led vote will make it harder for kids without reliable Internet access to complete their homework.
The Senate approved a Congressional Review Act (CRA)
resolution
to nullify the hotspot rule, which was issued by the Federal Communications Commission
in July 2024
under then-Chairwoman Jessica Rosenworcel. The program would be eliminated if the
House version
passes and President Trump signs the joint resolution of disapproval.
Senator Ted Cruz (R-Texas)
announced
the plan in January, saying the FCC program would "imped[e] parents' ability to decide what their kids see by subsidizing unsupervised access to inappropriate content." He also alleged that the hotspot program would shift control of Internet access from parents to schools and thus "heightens the risk of censoring kids' exposure to conservative viewpoints."
The Rosenworcel FCC's rule expanded E-Rate, a Universal Service Fund program,
allowing
schools and libraries to use E-Rate funding to lend out Wi-Fi hotspots and services that could be used off-premises. The FCC rule was titled, "Addressing the Homework Gap through the E-Rate Program," and the hotspot lending program was
scheduled to begin
in funding year 2025, which
starts in July 2025
.
Markey: “Cruel and shortsighted decision”
Today's Senate vote on the resolution of disapproval was 50–38. There was a 53–47
vote on Tuesday
that allowed the Senate measure to proceed to the final step. Sen. Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.)
said on Tuesday
that "this resolution would prevent millions of students, educators, and families from getting online."
"It would be a disgrace if we deprive those students and their families of this vast resource, of literally life-changing access to a really necessary service that helps them not just now but throughout their futures," Blumenthal said. "We ought to expand Internet access, not constrict it. We ought to be enhancing it, not cutting it off."
Blumenthal pointed out that under a joint resolution of disapproval, the FCC is forbidden to adopt a similar rule in the future. "I have to ask, really? Are schools and teachers crying out to repeal this rule? Really? No, they are not. How does this proposal make any sense for them or for families? For the parents? For the community? It makes no sense," Blumenthal said.
Sen. Edward Markey (D-Mass.)
called
the Republican move "a cruel and shortsighted decision that will widen the digital divide and rob kids of the tools they need to succeed."
FCC’s new chair opposed lending program
The FCC previously distributed Wi-Fi hotspots and other Internet access technology through the Emergency Connectivity Fund (ECF) that was authorized by Congress in 2021. After that program was axed last year, the FCC responded by adapting E-Rate to include hotspot lending.
FCC Chairman Brendan Carr, who was elevated to the agency's top spot by Trump in January, voted against the program last year. Carr said in his
dissent
that only Congress could decide whether to revive the hotspot lending.
"Now that the ECF program has expired, its future is up to Congress," he said at the time. "The legislative branch retains the power to decide whether to continue funding this Wi-Fi loaner program—or not. But Congress has made clear that the FCC's authority to fund this initiative is over."
Overall E-Rate funding is based on demand and
capped
at $4.94 billion per year. Actual spending for E-Rate in 2023 was
$2.48 billion
. E-Rate and other Universal Service Fund programs are paid for through fees imposed on phone companies, which generally pass the cost on to consumers.
The House version of the measure to kill the lending program was introduced by Rep. Russ Fulcher (R-Idaho). "E-Rate was designed to ensure schools and libraries have the connectivity they need to educate and serve their communities, not to create a backdoor entitlement program that stretches beyond the law's clear boundaries," Fulcher
said in February
when he filed the resolution. "The FCC cannot be allowed to unilaterally interpret the law in a way that fits their political agenda. The expansion of this program under the Biden administration was a blatant example of overreach that is not only unlawful but also disregards congressional intent."

data.title: Which countries have the best, and worst, living standards?
data.author: Manheim
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了2025年对193个国家的生活水平排名，显示全球人类发展几乎 everywhere 陷入停滞。文章指出，自新冠疫情爆发以来，医院爆满，学校和办公室关闭，经济停滞，而五年后的数据显示，生活水平的下滑可能持续。文章还提到其他相关话题，如俄罗斯的军事阅兵、教皇继任者预测、澳大利亚住房危机、以及国际贸易对美国制造业的影响等。总体而言，全球生活标准改善缓慢，许多地区面临持续挑战。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：各国生活质量评比的有效性和准确性

不同观点：
• **gumboshoes的观点**：对大国使用单一的生活质量评分不合理。他以美国为例，指出像康涅狄格州和密西西比州这样差异巨大的地区，用一个整体评分无法准确反映实际情况。

• **potbelly83的观点**：认为这些研究缺乏实际意义，特别指出澳大利亚不应排在前10。他认为，如果是租房者，生活质量不可能比在美国俄亥俄州外拥有大面积房产的技工更好。这暗示生活质量应根据住房状况等具体因素来评价，而非简单地以国家为单位。

补充讨论：
• **biglyburrito的观点**：未直接发表意见，但提供了一个存档链接，可能希望其他讨论者参考该链接以获取更多信息或背景资料。

• **marstall的观点**：对美国排名第17表示不满，虽然没有展开具体论据，但显然对美国的排名感到过低。

争议焦点：
• 争议的核心在于生活质量研究是否能够准确反映大国中不同地区和个体情况的差异。gumboshoes和potbelly83都对评比方法提出了质疑，认为这种单一维度的评分无法涵盖复杂多样的现实情况。

• 另一个争议点是国家排名的合理性，尤其是对大国如美国和澳大利亚的排名，讨论者对排名的实际意义和参考价值表示怀疑。

data.title: Alignment is not free: How model upgrades can silence your confidence signals
data.author: karinemellata
data.article_summary: 文章标题为“Monitor. Respond. Prevail. with Variance”，介绍了一款名为Variance的工具，帮助用户监控、响应并最终战胜各种挑战。Variance提供实时监控和快速响应功能，旨在提高工作效率和团队协作能力。文章强调通过使用该工具，用户可以更好地管理任务和项目，确保问题得到及时解决，从而在竞争中保持优势。文章还邀请读者立即开始使用Variance，以体验其带来的高效和便捷。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OpenAI模型对齐（alignment）与创造力、精度之间的关系，以及是否应该开发无审查的LLM模型。

不同观点：
• Centigonal认为，文章中从“在4.1-mini版本中丢失了信心信号”直接推导出“这是由于对齐/可控性改进造成的”缺乏足够的解释。他质疑是如何确定对齐是原因的，特别是考虑到模型蒸馏可能会破坏熵信号。

• Behnamoh支持对齐可能限制模型创造力的观点，并引用了一篇论文（https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.05587）作为证据。他将这种情况类比为人类在言论受限时会变得更保守，无法表达各种想法。

• Qwertytyyuu对人们在高精度系统中使用LLM表示担忧，暗示对齐和审查可能影响模型的可靠性。

• Erwin-co提出为何不开发一个完全无审查的LLM，认为这样可能使模型更“智能”，暗示对齐过程限制了模型的潜力。

• User_7832以讽刺的口吻评论文章本身读起来像是由一个低质量LLM写的，质疑文章内容的质量和可信度。

• Sega_sai建议模型可以返回一个概率，反映其陈述的准确性，以此提高模型的透明度和可信度。

• Rusk简短评论，认为这些变化和升级是常态，暗示对持续的模型改进并不惊讶。

• Gotoeleven以幽默的方式评论关于对齐使LLM变“笨”的文章，并提出一种技术解决方案：将对齐/去偏见作为独立于核心模型的二次过滤器，以保持核心模型的“现实”建模能力。他指出实现这一方案的难点在于获取合适的数据和考虑用户身份。

补充讨论：
• 对齐（alignment）和模型创造力之间的关系是争议的焦点，部分评论认为对齐限制了模型的表现和自由表达。
• 关于是否应开发无审查的LLM存在不同意见，一部分人认为无审查模型可能更智能或更自由，但另一部分人对其潜在风险表示担忧。
• 技术解决方案如二次过滤器被提出，以平衡模型的智能性和社会责任。

data.title: Gemini 2.5 Pro Preview
data.author: meetpateltech
data.article_summary: Google发布了Gemini 2.5 Pro Preview版，主要提升了编码性能，特别在前端和UI开发方面表现更佳。该版本在代码转换、编辑及复杂工作流创建上也有显著改进，并在WebDev Arena排行榜上排名第一。新版在视频理解和功能开发上表现突出，能将视频转化为学习应用，并自动生成新功能和UI组件。开发者可通过Google AI Studio的Gemini API使用该版本，企业用户可通过Vertex AI使用。更新后的模型解决了函数调用错误问题，且价格不变。Google期待看到开发者利用新模型创造的应用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Gemini 2.5模型的性能、应用及其相关问题

不同观点：
• [segphault] 认为Gemini 2.5模型在编程中表现显著提升，特别是在减少虚构API方面，能够替代搜索和StackOverflow，但仍无法像人类一样处理抽象和架构问题。
• [paulirish] 指出Gemini 2.5 Pro在WebDev Arena的排名存在局限性，该竞技场主要针对React和Tailwind技术，对其他框架如Vanilla JS支持不佳，可能导致模型竞争的狭义定义问题。
• [ranyume] 抱怨Gemini 2.5生成的代码包含过多注释，影响了使用体验。
• [laborcontract] 认为Gemini 2.5在代码差异编辑方面表现优异，但在生成完美匹配的代码差异上仍有不足，并对免费层的更新和模型命名提出疑问。
• [mohsen1] 通过对比基准测试数据指出Gemini 2.5在多个领域仍落后于o3模型。

补充讨论：
• [andy12_] 发现Gemini 2.5新版本在某些基准测试中得分略低，但在LiveCodeBench上有所提升。
• [planb] 和 [killerstorm] 对模型的命名方式表示困惑和不满，建议采用更直观的版本号命名。
• [herpdyderp] 认为尽管模型表现良好，但用户界面仍存在问题，并分享了使用技巧。
• [arnaudsm] 认为新模型在多个基准测试中表现不如旧版本，怀疑是由于训练过程中的问题。
• [ionwake] 询问如何在Cursor中使用Gemini 2.5模型，并对模型支持情况表示关注。
• [minzi] 对Gemini的网页应用用户体验不满，认为Google在UI方面落后，赞扬Claude的网页应用功能更完善。
• [franze] 分享了使用Gemini模型进行创意项目的心得，并对结果表示满意。
• [simonw] 使用Gemini 2.5模型生成帖子评论摘要，对其表现给予积极评价，并提供了具体示例和脚本。
• [siwakotisaurav] 对Gemini 2.5在WebDev Arena排名第一表示惊讶，但认为Claude在个人经验中仍表现更好。

争议焦点：
• Gemini 2.5模型在WebDev Arena的排名和其对特定技术的支持局限性引发讨论，部分用户认为该排名不能全面反映模型实际能力。
• 模型命名和版本更新策略引发用户困惑和不满，建议采用更直观的版本号命名方式。
• 用户对模型生成代码中包含过多注释的问题表示不满，认为影响了代码的可读性和使用体验。

总结：
Gemini 2.5模型在编程任务中表现出色，但在用户界面、命名策略和特定技术支持方面仍存在改进空间，部分用户对其基准测试表现和实际应用效果持不同看法。

Gemini
Gemini 2.5 Pro Preview: even better coding performance
MAY 6, 2025
Logan Kilpatrick
Senior Product Manager
Gemini API and Google AI Studio
Share
Facebook
Twitter
LinkedIn
Mail
We’ve seen developers doing amazing things with
Gemini 2.5 Pro
, so we decided to release an updated version a couple of weeks early to get into developers hands sooner.
Today we’re excited to release Gemini 2.5 Pro Preview (I/O edition). This update features even stronger coding capabilities, for you to start building with before Google I/O later this month. Expect meaningful improvements for front-end and UI development, alongside improvements in fundamental coding tasks such as transforming and editing code, and creating sophisticated agentic workflows.
“We found Gemini 2.5 Pro to be the best frontier model when it comes to "capability over latency" ratio. I look forward to rolling it out on Replit Agent whenever a latency-sensitive task needs to be accomplished with a high degree of reliability.”
–
Michele Catasta, President,
Replit
Best-in-class frontend web development
Gemini 2.5 Pro now ranks #1 on the
WebDev Arena leaderboard
, which measures human preference for a model’s ability to build aesthetically pleasing and functional web apps. Drawing on this leading capability, Gemini 2.5 Pro powers Cursor’s innovative code agent and empowers our collaborations with companies like Cognition and Replit. Together, we're pushing the frontiers of agentic programming to unlock new possibilities for developers.
“The updated Gemini 2.5 Pro achieves leading performance on our junior-dev evals. It was the first-ever model that solved one of our evals involving a larger refactor of a request routing backend. It felt like a more senior developer because it was able to make correct judgement calls and choose good abstractions.”
–
Silas Alberti, Founding Team,
Cognition
Gemini 2.5 Pro in action
Gemini 2.5 Pro’s deep understanding of code, combined with powerful reasoning, continues to make Gemini 2.5 Pro the go-to model for developers. We’re particularly excited about how this model can be used in the following cases.
Video to code
Gemini 2.5 Pro delivers state-of-the-art video understanding, scoring 84.8% on the VideoMME benchmark. Combining this with coding enables new flows that were previously not possible with previous versions. For example, the
Video to Learning App
in Google AI Studio demonstrates how Gemini 2.5 Pro creates an interactive learning app based on a single YouTube video. With improved video understanding and complete UI, the updated Gemini 2.5 Pro model delivers a more functional experience than the previous simple example.
Link to Youtube Video
(visible only when JS is disabled)
Easier feature development
Gemini 2.5 Pro is strong at front-end web development, helping you get more done. Implementing new features means manually diving into design files and inspecting components to match style properties like colors, fonts, padding, margins, and borders then manually writing the CSS code needed to replicate those visual properties accurately. Now imagine using Gemini 2.5 Pro in an IDE and having the model generate new features, like adding a video player in the style of the other apps in the
Gemini 95
starter app.
Link to Youtube Video
(visible only when JS is disabled)
Quick concepts to working apps
Bringing ideas to life with both functionality and a beautiful UI is made easier with Gemini 2.5 Pro. The new
dictation starter app
, built using the updated model, is a great example of this in action. Pay attention to some of the details like the wavelength animations, responsive design, and subtle button hover effects. By default, the model has a real taste for aesthetic web development while maintaining its steerability, helping developers quickly take a concept to a working web app. Gemini 2.5 Pro was able to design and code the microphone UI animation for the dictation starter app.
Link to Youtube Video
(visible only when JS is disabled)
Start building with Gemini 2.5 Pro
You can build with Gemini 2.5 Pro with the Gemini API in
Google AI Studio
, and enterprise customers can use
Vertex AI
.
For developers already using Gemini 2.5 Pro, this new version will not only improve coding performance but will also address key developer feedback including reducing errors in function calling and improving function calling trigger rates. The previous iteration (03-25) now points to the most recent version (05-06), so no action is required to use the improved model, and it continues to be available at the same
price
. We have also
updated the model card
with the new version of 2.5 Pro .
We can’t wait to see the amazing apps you build!
